Table 2 lists 301 neuron-only, seven astrocyte-only, ten Sox2-only, fifteen Sox2-plus-neuron, one neuron-plus-astrocyte and twenty-nine undetermined clusters, totaling 363 across fifty-four hemispheres. Figure S4 traverses optical depth in micrometres, not elapsed time. The radial-process example is a fixed mixed cluster, not observation of its founder or a conversion event. Running Methods specifies seven transgenic runners and seven wild-type littermate controls, but Figure 5 shows and counts GFP-positive cells in both groups. The comparison uses individual cages with or without wheel access, seven daily 100 mg/kg BrdU injections and collection twenty-four hours after the last injection; the route is unreported. GFP counting is described as blind; full animal allocation, raw measurements and multiplicity-adjusted analyses are unavailable.

Reported GFP-density comparisons have P=0.1724, n=7 for total reporter cells and P=0.1125, n=5 for radial cells. These nonsignificant comparisons do not establish equivalence, conservation of whole-population counts or a constant pool through time. The control-genotype conflict also applies to these nulls.

Figure 6 models population maintenance and possible radial/nonradial lineage relations. Its caption explicitly distinguishes asymmetric contribution at population level from asymmetric division of individual cells. Birth, death, survival, marker kinetics and a regulated feedback variable are not jointly measured; no universal stem-cell minimum or closed homeostatic construction is established.

Three is therefore a restricted representation-theoretic minimum, not a measured particle population or sufficient formation condition.

Compare source gene-addition and deletion derivatives of JCVI-syn3.0 and JCVI-syn3A in supplied SP4 medium, using bulk optical area distributions, representative microscopy and microfluidic morphology. Keep ectopic addition to syn3.0 distinct from deletion in the larger syn3A background.

Adding seven source genes together restores a nearly normal morphology in the JCVI-syn3.0 background; the ftsZ-containing cluster alone does not. Within the tested syn3.0+126 background, removing any of the seven returns pleomorphism.

JCVI-syn3A retains nearly normal morphology after deletion of the ftsZ-containing cluster, despite that cluster being required in the tested syn3.0+126 context. The observed requirement is conditional on genomic and expression context, not a universal seven-gene minimum for life.
In the existing JCVI-syn3.0 genome, the source seven-gene addition/deletion comparison changes the morphological phenotype, while single-cluster addition is insufficient.

In living wild-type yeast, compare six GFP-Protein A reporter variants of approximately 27-67 kDa. Bleach cytoplasm and fit nuclear fluorescence equilibration using measured cell/nuclear geometry and an assumed NPC surface density; the source reports 236 wild-type single-cell measurements across the series.

The measured reporter-size series shows progressively slower passive exchange without a sharp mass cutoff. Source normalized time constants are 15 +/- 1.4 s for 27 kDa GFP and 413 +/- 92 s for the 67 kDa reporter, with source 95% confidence intervals.

The source normalizes passive exchange through a compartmental Fick-law model using nuclear/cytoplasmic volumes and estimated pore numbers. Size-dependent exchange is an inferred permeability under these assumptions, not direct counting of individual nuclear-pore crossings.

Compare purified QUEEN variants and reporter-expressing E. coli, keeping cell-suspension/luciferase calibration and continuous-culture growth controls separate. The source QUEEN controls reduce growth-rate-dependent bias relative to the tested FRET reporters, while residual in-vivo/in-vitro differences require correction. Acidified cells below the reported pH-insensitive range can bias QUEEN-2m estimates.

Observe QUEEN-2m-expressing E. coli from glucose-limited aerated continuous culture at 25 C, immobilized under the source agarose film. Convert single-cell 405/480 excitation ratios to estimated ATP using the source calibration and noise correction; images are single observations per cell, not ATP time courses.

The source estimates an asymmetric ATP distribution with mean 1.54 mM and standard deviation 1.22 mM in its selected culture. These are population distribution statistics after source correction, not universal cellular values or uncertainty of a common ATP concentration.

The source proposes variation in enzyme content as a possible cause of ATP heterogeneity but does not establish that mechanism. Similar ATP/ADP ratios across cells remain possible even when ATP concentrations differ.

In source S. cerevisiae derivatives cultured in synthetic dropout medium at 30 C, compare source-designated constitutive rtTA and positive-autoregulatory circuits, with chromosomal GFP reporters or direct rtTA-GFP fusion. Vary inducer and gene dosage; examine fluorescence 6-12 h after induction. Keep promoter, reporter placement and copy-number variants distinct.

The source constitutive-activator circuits give graded unimodal responses, whereas the positive-feedback variants produce separated low/high GFP populations over tested induction conditions. Reporter placement and gene dosage change peak separation and the fractions in each state.

In the selected autoregulatory preparation, the source reports stable population fractions during its 6-12 h examination interval; removing the inducer causes expression to decay toward uninduced levels. The observation does not establish irreversible cell identity.

The source mathematical model offers bistability as an interpretation of the synthetic positive-feedback data; its kinetics/noise assumptions and illustrative cooperativity are not independently fitted here. Positive feedback need not give binary behavior for all parameter regimes.
Within the tested engineered yeast circuit family, replacing source-designated constitutive activator expression with positive autoregulation changes the single-cell reporter response distribution.

Follow induced source ABY001 on- and off-cells on agarose containing the same inducer. Inspect colony descendants by fluorescence; retain the source Figure 5 caption times of 16 h for the illustrated off-derived colony and 22 h for the on-derived colony separately from the main prose 16 h description.

Initially low-expression cells can produce mixed low/high colonies under continued induction, while the illustrated high-expression lineage retains detectable reporter expression. The source reports slower growth of high-expressing cells, but the inconsistent image times prevent a new precise relative division-rate estimate.

Compare source HeLa cells expressing dynab alone, dynamin-1 or dynamin-2 alone, corresponding coexpressions and nontransfected controls. Measure fluorescent transferrin after the 30 min uptake interval and acid removal of surface ligand; use intracellular image intensity and separate transferrin-receptor immunofluorescence.

Dynab alone or coexpressed with dynamin-2 markedly reduces source transferrin internalization and redistributes detectable receptor toward the cell surface; coexpression with dynamin-1 preserves uptake relative to the tested dynamin-overexpression controls.
In the measured HeLa transferrin assay, dynab and dynamin isoform coexpression alter intracellular uptake relative to the named controls.

Use the source HeLa expression variants in the separate low-EGF fluorescent uptake assay, followed by acid removal of surface ligand and EGFR immunofluorescence. Do not equate the different ligand concentration, receptor or cells with the transferrin experiment.

In the source low-EGF assay, dynab has only a minor effect on EGF internalization and does not show the transferrin-receptor redistribution pattern. The response of one endocytic cargo is insufficient to describe all uptake.

In source HeLa cells, compare tagged clathrin with EGFP control or dynab using live TIRF imaging. The embedded Figure 4 supplement 1 pools 234 and 236 events, respectively, from four experiments with one to five cells per experiment.

The source reports no significant change in clathrin-pit lifetime under its dynab/control comparison, while its separate transferrin experiment detects impaired internalization. Unchanged pit timing is therefore insufficient to certify unperturbed cargo transport.

Follow source fluorescent cargo released from ER aggregates by ligand in modified S. cerevisiae at approximately 23 C. Compare absent/APVNTT/APVNTA export-signal variants and ERV29 versus erv29 deletion, retaining the engineered pdr1/pdr3 and vps10 background. Quantify perinuclear ER fluorescence and endoglycosidase-sensitive mobility.

The APV-containing signal accelerates source reporter ER exit to a reported approximately 7.5 min half-time; removing Erv29 returns slow bulk-flow-like exit. Eliminating the glycosylation signal does not remove rapid ER exit, separating receptor-linked export from glycosylation.

The source APVNTT cargo shows an endoglycosidase-H-sensitive mobility difference relative to its nonglycosylated variant. This supports N-linked modification of the chosen reporter, not exhaustive maturation or folding of all exported proteins.
For the supplied engineered yeast cargo, the APV signal/Erv29 comparison changes measured ER-exit kinetics, while the glycosylation-site variant retains rapid exit.

Track individual source yeast Golgi cisternae by three-color 4D confocal microscopy after release of engineered fluorescent cargo, using early Vrg4 and late Sec7 markers. The ordinary maturation observations are kept separate from nocodazole-treated daughter-cell FRAP experiments.

Individual source cisternae lose early Vrg4, acquire late Sec7 and subsequently lose Sec7 over approximately three minutes, while cargo remains visible through maturation. Functional compartment organization does not require immutable molecular membership.

Across 19 aligned source maturation events, cargo fluorescence transiently increases by approximately 70% during the early-to-late transition. This intensity result motivates an exchange interpretation but is not by itself direct counting of transported molecules.

Use source nocodazole-treated yeast mothers and daughters. After cargo release, bleach daughter cargo fluorescence while preserving resident Golgi markers and follow recovery at maturation; compare AP-1 Apl4 deletion or nonglycosylated reporter with the designated controls.

The source control cisternae recover cargo fluorescence around the early-to-late transition; AP-1 disruption or removal of the reporter glycosylation site largely eliminates the recovery and transient increase, while Golgi maturation remains observed.

The source proposes that glycosylated soluble cargo can accompany transmembrane glycosylation enzymes in AP-1 carriers. The actual cargo-enzyme binding and individual recycling carriers were not directly established by this source readout.
In the source nocodazole/FRAP preparation, AP-1 disruption or loss of reporter glycosylation suppresses the measured cargo recovery at the maturation transition.

After ligand-triggered cargo release, compare cell-associated and medium fractions from source engineered yeast in rich glucose medium by immunoblotting; contrast the source minimal-medium observation, where cell-wall/periplasm retention and fluorescence quenching are relevant.

The source reporter is detected in rich medium by approximately ten minutes and more prominently at twenty minutes. No medium signal was detected in the separate minimal-medium experiment, despite evidence for periplasmic reporter accumulation; absence from collected medium is not equivalent to absence of secretion.

The source follows cargo departure from late Golgi but could not track post-Golgi carriers or their final fusion at the plasma membrane. Detailed targeting, docking, fusion and release mechanisms remain unestablished by this acquisition.

Compare source HEK293T F8-S2 nuclease-exposed populations with control backbone or donor template, retaining two guide clones and unselected versus approximately two-week drug-selected pools. The source detects different target-alteration fractions according to transfected-cell selection, donor availability, guide clone and assay. For the source selected F8-S2 conditions, the adjacent-probe analysis assigns approximately 43% of the inferred break outcomes to donor-associated HDR. This is a source inference dependent on probe design and normalization, not a universal cellular HDR probability or guaranteed restoration of native sequence.

The reviewed targeted-break assays do not establish total endogenous lesion repair, replication-error correction, chromatin-state control, checkpoint coordination, apoptosis selection or faithful genome inheritance over many generations. Those broader claims require separate lesion- and lineage-specific studies.

In cultured COS-7 cells imaged at 37 C, compare ER-marker/tubulin live images with the separate STIM1 tip-associated readout. Use source peripheral regions and pre/post-nocodazole windows; sliding and tip-attachment events have distinct operational definitions.

After source hyperacetylation treatment, sliding also occurs on straighter microtubules. Untreated curvature/acetylation association therefore does not identify geometric curvature as a universal prerequisite for sliding.
Under the declared COS-7 treatment and imaging conditions, TSA and the separate tubacin comparison increase measured ER sliding with increased acetylation-associated signal.

Use separate source COS-7 preparations labeled for ER plus mitochondria or ER plus Rab5-positive early endosomes. Combine live imaging and retrospective tubulin/acetylation staining in cell peripheries; the organelle comparisons are not one simultaneous same-cell acquisition.

In the source untreated samples, 77% of 57 mitochondria from ten cells colocalize with acetylated microtubules. Only 14% of 426 early endosomes from five cells show that colocalization, despite frequent ER association. The denominators and distinct preparations are retained.

The source live imaging shows ER-mitochondrial and ER-endosomal overlaps persisting during movement. This supports dynamic spatial organization within the optical observation window, not permanent anchoring or proof of all molecular contacts.

The observed organelle preferences and drug responses do not uniquely determine a cell-scale downward causal law, molecular-signaling efficiency, division inheritance, or the causal role of each contact in lipid/calcium exchange.

Keep newly sequenced Paulinella longichromatophora and P. micropora NZ27 chromatophore genomes distinct from three previously deposited comparator genomes. Assemble and annotate source sequence data; the source species differ in collection, genome preparation and sequencing platform.

Analyze source chromatophore/cyanobacterial/plastid ortholog comparisons, keeping the 406-gene cyanobacterial/chromatophore tree distinct from the twenty-gene forty-genome Fig. 2 analysis. Infer gene-family ancestors by parsimony and dates through the source externally calibrated molecular clock.

Reconstructed ancestral inventories, early rapid loss and later slower loss are historical inferences, not a witnessed transformation or automatically repeatable construction protocol.

These chromatophore comparisons do not establish a single mandatory sequence for all mitochondria, plastids and cellular compartments. Exact extinct donor, host state, universal event order, inheritance control and sufficient construction conditions remain outside the reviewed evidence.

In Paulinella chromatophora CCAC0185, prepare chromatophore lysates from three independent cultures and enrich protein N-termini by HUNTER for LC-MS/MS. Assign peptides with source transcriptome/chromatophore reference sequences, keeping detected protein processing distinct from bioinformatic transit-motif prediction.

The source identifies N-termini for 132 chromatophore-encoded and 76 nucleus-encoded proteins. Of 37 nuclear proteins carrying the source transit-peptide annotation, thirty show processing in a common region; most retain the second transit-peptide part.

Transit motifs, predicted helices and processing patterns motivate the source Golgi/AP-1 trafficking model, but do not directly demonstrate the complete route. Processing peptidase identity and translocation across the inner chromatophore membrane remain unknown.

In the source PROPS-expressing E. coli preparation under an agarose pad and minimal medium, compare optical voltage responses with coexpressed cytoplasmic pHluorin and metabolic/illumination perturbations. Calibration is based on induced transmembrane voltage; full strain/preparation details are in the unread supplement.

The source separates voltage-sensitive and pH-sensitive signals. Membrane voltage alone is not a measured concentration gradient for every solute, a complete proton-motive-force budget or a globally constant cellular state.

The source proposes voltage-regulated cationic efflux and discusses lowered thermodynamic barriers during depolarization. The data do not uniquely distinguish a particular active efflux system, changing permeability, passive redistribution or their combination.

Reconstruct prokaryotic organization through existing genomically minimized mycoplasmas: separate membrane enclosure, population propagation, complete scission, reporter expression and genotype-dependent morphology. Reconstruct endosymbiotic organization through contemporary Paulinella chromatophore protein processing and comparative genome evidence. Distinguish extant host/organelle coordination, annotated functional dependence, historical reconstruction and proposed import mechanisms; do not turn evolutionary origin into a repeatable universal construction recipe.

Preserve the untracked late-carrier/fusion steps and the hypothetical soluble-cargo packaging mechanism.

Reconstruct cell-scale spatial organization as finite ER/mitochondrion/endosome localization and movement under specified microtubule-state perturbations. Follow sister cells expressing caspase/MOMP reporters after uniform TRAIL exposure; compare division-to-treatment interval, protein-synthesis inhibition and Bid overexpression with adopted model predictions.
Closely related cells initially have more similar response times than unrelated cells, but this resemblance decays; protein-state variability and history matter even within clonal populations.
Compare related and unrelated cells and perturb protein production or Bid level.

Expose primary mouse liver cells to 4.5 percent ethanol for the main same-cell 2.5-hour imaging experiment, remove inducer and follow the same cells. The 5-hour population experiment is a distinct comparison; no HeLa caspase result is transferred to these cells.
Primary liver cells exhibiting apoptotic morphology and mitochondrial fragmentation can recover those appearances after ethanol removal in the source same-cell experiment.
Remove the defined apoptotic inducer and observe the same previously responding cells.

Introduce doxycycline-inducible neuronal-factor lentiviruses into mouse fibroblasts, screen factor combinations and assay neuronal markers, morphology and whole-cell electrophysiology. Functional synapse tests include source-defined co-cultures.
Defined transcription-factor combinations can generate cells with neuronal functional readouts from fibroblast cultures; marker expression and electrical function are distinct measured endpoints.

Collect ICM cells from E3.25-E4.5 mouse embryos, perform single-cell amplification/qPCR and microarray profiling, and compare staged wild-type with Fgf4-null embryos. The main wild-type microarray map contains 66 selected single cells.

Lineage expression separation emerges progressively, while Fgf4-null profiles show impaired EPI/PrE segregation relative to wild type; initial expression variability and later signal reinforcement are distinguished.
Compare staged embryos and Fgf4-null versus wild-type ICM profiles.

Mix L929 sender cells bearing CD19 with synNotch receiver cells that induce E-cadherin/GFP, then follow fluorescence and spatial sorting. Reciprocal ligand circuits form a separate three-layer program.

Use pHluorin fluorescence with the source calibration, buffered medium and growth measurements. Compare batch growth, medium exchange, deletion mutants and PMA1-related perturbations.

Compare controlled nutrient-limited chemostats using metabolite/protein abundance measurements, external rates and constrained metabolic flux analysis. SIMMER compares kinetic forms; selected predicted inhibitors receive separate biochemical tests.

Substrate and metabolite levels account for substantial flux variation across the tested conditions; selected allosteric inhibition is biochemically supported, whereas broader rate-control assignments depend on model and available measurements.
Change the limiting nutrient and compare source-inferred flux and candidate kinetic regulation.
Compare glucose starvation, AMPK perturbation, Rheb/mTORC1 activity and Ulk1 mutants using immunoprecipitation, phosphosite blots, in-vitro kinase assays and source autophagy readouts.

Change AMPK/mTOR activity or Ulk1 phosphorylation context under defined nutrient conditions.

Change the nutrient combination or activate AMPK with source-defined pharmacology.

Inhibit mTORC1 pharmacologically and compare the IL1A bypass condition.

Wash out ethanol after the defined reporter-positive response.

Delete Atg7 in the specified Pax7-expressing satellite-cell preparation.

Restoring autophagy-related activity improves source-reported proliferative/regenerative behavior of geriatric satellite cells in these finite assays; this response differs from rapamycin-treated arrested fibroblasts and Atg7-null cells.
Pretreat geriatric donor cells with rapamycin or the separately defined Atg7-expression intervention.

Apply the source-defined antioxidant treatment to the geriatric preparation.

Nutrient-limited chemostat conditions yield different measured metabolite/protein profiles and extracellular rates, supplying inputs for the separate source flux/kinetic inference.
Change the supplied limiting nutrient and controlled culture growth conditions.

Cellular signaling is reconstructed as stimulus-dependent molecular/cellular response in bacterial, yeast and mammalian preparations, with timing, amplification, attenuation and feedback measured separately.

A cell-wide interpretation is a synthesis over defined assays, not proof of complete integrated control, cellular understanding, adaptation optimality or a universal eukaryotic/prokaryotic prerequisite.
Proliferation/quiescence control, cell-free mitotic switching, DNA-damage-dependent arrest and receptor-mediated apoptotic execution are distinct processes that can interact in particular cells.

Cell-cycle regulation and apoptosis are not one obligatory process shared by every cell. Neither prokaryotic ancestry, allostery in every control step nor a universal irreversible termination threshold is derived from these experiments.
Natural embryonic lineage expression separation and engineered fibroblast-to-neuron functional conversion provide different evidence for cellular state diversification.

Shared lineage/genetic background does not prove complete sequence identity; lentiviral conversion explicitly changes the construct context. Persistent identity, epigenetic inheritance, metabolic specialization and signaling responsiveness require distinct endpoint evidence.
Homeostasis is represented by named regulated variables and finite recovery responses: osmotic signaling/volume, cytosolic pH, heat-shock feedback and nutrient-dependent quality-control responses.

No unique fixed viable envelope, simultaneous stabilization of all variables, universally beneficial stress response or general recovery guarantee is measured. Redox and every ion-specific mechanism remain separate evidence obligations.
Cell contact, engineered juxtacrine induction, differential adhesion and multicellular spatial sorting are separated from natural lineage signaling and from physiological tissue differentiation.

An engineered aggregate is not a universal evolutionary prototissue stage. No gap-junction conductance, general neighbor synchronization, complete tissue function or universal two-cell critical number is measured.

Regulatory networks are represented by preparation-specific feedback, switching, input waveform and response constraints across Hsp70, Hog1, CDK2, apoptosis, transcription-factor and metabolic assays.

A drawn motif alone does not establish its dynamic function. These local/mesoscopic network studies do not reconstruct one complete cell-wide controller, every coupling strength or a universal robustness theorem.

Sensing is represented by ligand-dependent bacterial pathway activity, yeast osmotic response and stress/nutrient-response signaling, with adaptation distinguished from initial detection and later viability.

A sensory pathway can also change behavior, as in chemotaxis; excluding behavioral action is an editorial boundary, not a biological law. No universal optimization, toxin-sensing mechanism or perfect adaptation to arbitrary inputs is established.
Metabolite availability, pH, kinase state and compartment-associated signaling can condition biochemical activity and inferred pathway flux in specified cellular preparations.

The cell-state description summarizes physically realized variables. The assays do not establish an additional irreducible downward force, coordinated purpose, universal metabolic-cycle necessity or causation from a global state label alone.
Apoptotic execution is represented by molecular network perturbations, mitochondrial/caspase dynamics, response heterogeneity and a separate inducer-washout recovery counterexample.

Molecules do not have autonomous survival goals. A whole-cell commitment label is not an extra intervention. Execution signs do not universally preclude recovery, and local viability/repair capability was not exhaustively measured before death.

Autophagy is represented by regulated initiation, lysosomal degradation/flux constraints and a selective mitochondrial-turnover preparation, with markers, cargo elimination and molecular reuse distinguished.

LC3/puncta are not alone completed flux. Chaperone participation, mTOR input and prokaryotic organization are not universal prerequisites for every degradation pathway. Direct atom-level recycling and every cargo-recognition mechanism remain unmeasured.
mTOR/AMPK regulation of Ulk1/autophagy and mTOR-sensitive senescent secretion are distinct preparation-specific regulatory processes; senescence growth arrest is an independent endpoint.

Nutrient classes, cell backgrounds, serum and observation times change the autophagy outcome. Rapamycin-sensitive SASP does not demonstrate rejuvenation, recovery of division or a universal maintenance-versus-growth decision variable.
The source infers effective integral feedback and constrains its location, but the complete molecular realization of the integrating reactions remains unidentified in this reconstruction.
Opposite autophagy outcomes in the Kim2011 and Nwadike2018 preparations require matched nutrient, serum, cell-background, time and flux comparisons before a common causal rule can be assigned.

A coarse-grained cell-state description may organize physical rate dependence, but an independently identifiable higher-level causal effect requires specified interventions, mediators, alternatives and aggregation assumptions.

Lgr5/Olfm4 cells proliferate and generate long-term villus progeny in the reported Paneth-depleted Atoh1 backgrounds. This is a counterexample to unconditional Paneth-cell necessity, with explicit genetic bypass and missing-secretory-lineage limits; it does not refute every form of environmental stem-cell support.

Give three clodronate-liposome intravenous injections over four days before amputation to maximize monocyte/macrophage depletion, compared with PBS liposomes. Assess early blastema/proliferation and later limb regrowth, collagen histology and alpha-SMA. Source early-depleted animals fail regrowth, including scars examined at 30/90 days and some follow-up to 150 days; replenishment alone does not restart the closed stump.

The source maximally depletes monocyte/macrophage populations before adult axolotl limb injury, against control liposomes; this is an existing-organism perturbation, not a phylogenetic origin experiment.

The wound closes while blastema formation/regrowth fails and collagen-rich, alpha-SMA-associated fibrotic tissue persists. Early functional repair, preserved viability and complete anatomical regeneration are not interchangeable outcomes.

Give three clodronate-liposome injections during days 10-13 after limb resection, after midbud blastema formation, and compare progression through source-defined stages with control regeneration. Keep this intervention window separate from preamputation maximal depletion.
After an established blastema, macrophage depletion permits eventual regeneration with a delay. The same broad cell-class perturbation can have different outcome severity depending on when it occurs.

After initial early-depletion regenerative failure and subsequent endogenous macrophage replenishment, reamputate at a more proximal position including a functional nerve transection. Follow new limb regrowth; source Figure 6 describes six animals and the main text includes failed stumps up to 150 days before renewed injury.
The source creates a new proximal wound after the phagocyte population has returned, rather than simply adding one identified molecule to the old wound.

Previously failed stumps can regenerate after renewed proximal amputation in a replenished context. This shows retained regenerative competence under changed conditions without demonstrating that macrophage repopulation alone erases a stable scar.

The main Results and Figures 1-2 describe cardiomyocyte-specific Cre/lox labeling at 48 hpf, followed by growth to adulthood (approximately three months/sexual maturity) before ventricular resection and myocardium assessment at 7, 14 and 30 days. The general Methods summary separately describes induction in embryos/adults with at least one week of washout; that general method is not substituted for the displayed embryonically induced series. Remove approximately one fifth of the adult ventricle and combine lineage label with sarcomeric markers, separately reported BrdU incorporation and electron microscopy of 5/7-day tissue. Uninjured hearts provide structural/proliferation comparisons.

Regenerated zebrafish ventricular myocardium retains the pre-injury cardiomyocyte label induced at 48 hpf in the displayed lineage series, with DNA synthesis and locally disorganized sarcomeres during adult rebuilding. The source supports limited dedifferentiation within a lineage rather than compulsory recruitment from a general stem-cell niche; this is not a separately reconstructed adult-only induction experiment.

Following adult ventricular resection, recover for 24 hours, then compare 3 micromolar cyclapolin-9 in system water with the source control, replacing water/treatment daily. Follow the 30-day recovery interval, myocardium replacement, BrdU-labeled cardiomyocytes and TUNEL. The separate embryonic ablation assay is excluded from this adult context.
The source changes the adult injury-recovery environment with cyclapolin-9 compared with its control; embryonic chemical ablation is not treated as the same preparation.

Cyclapolin-9 reduces labeled cardiomyocyte DNA-synthesis/regeneration readouts in the adult source comparison. The result supports a bounded drug-sensitive contribution to rebuilding, not an independently proven universal kinase necessity or all-genome-repair bundle.

Serum-starve confluent Swiss 3T3 cultures, then compare serum/LPA stimulation with C3-mediated Rho inhibition, contractility inhibitors or active-Rho microinjection. Add exogenous fibronectin; quantify fibrils, radiolabeled binding and detergent-insoluble incorporation. The source reports maximal visible fibril assembly near 4-6 hours after LPA, while binding and long-term incorporation use distinct assay durations.
The source uses loss-of-function, pharmacological and active-Rho comparisons to alter contractile conditions in fibroblasts supplied with fibronectin.

Fibrillar/insoluble fibronectin assembly increases with the source's stimulatory conditions and is suppressed by the tested Rho/contractility interventions. Protein production, binding, fibrillar organization and insoluble incorporation remain distinct readouts.

Immobilize fibronectin on stretchable rubber, apply the source's approximately 30-35 percent extension and compare binding of soluble fibronectin, the 70-kDa amino-terminal fragment and the L8 antibody with unstretched/control-antibody conditions. Keep this cell-free surface experiment separate from cellular fibril assembly and from a purified free-solution protein-folding assay.
The source externally stretches immobilized fibronectin without cells and compares binding with the corresponding unstretched surface.

Stretch enhances binding of tested fibronectin/fragment and the L8 epitope-sensitive antibody in the cell-free preparation. This supports a bounded conformational-accessibility interpretation separate from total protein abundance or a full molecular unfolding trajectory.

Overlay type-I collagen onto existing polarized MDCK monolayers. Compare beta1-integrin antibody AIIB2 with control antibody and induced dominant-negative/active Rac1 backgrounds. Measure Rac1-GTP within minutes/hours and tubulocyst architecture after several days; the source shows transient Rac1 activation, not a continuously elevated signal.
Collagen is presented to the existing apical surface with matched integrin/Rac1 manipulations; without overlay, tested monolayers can remain polarized.

The source detects an early Rac1 response and later tubulocyst formation that are altered by beta1/Rac1 perturbations. The result supports spatial coordination with the matrix while preserving the distinction between possessing polarity and orienting it in tissue geometry.

Embed single MDCK cells in collagen and grow for about 7-10 days. Compare 8 micrograms/ml AIIB2 with control conditions, and separately supplement laminin-1 or collagen IV or induce active Rac1. Score luminal versus peripheral gp135/beta-catenin orientation, lumen morphology and extracellular laminin organization; synthesis/secretion assays distinguish abundance from assembly. Numeric collagen concentrations with unresolved displayed units are excluded.
The source compares beta1-blocked cysts with laminin-1, collagen-IV and active-Rac1 conditions; matrix constituents are not interchangeable generic structural support.

AIIB2 cysts retain polarized domains with inverted orientation and disorganized laminin despite no measured decrease in overall laminin synthesis/secretion. Laminin-1 and active Rac1 improve interior orientation under their conditions; collagen IV does not, and lumen architecture can remain incompletely restored.

Culture low-passage human mesenchymal stromal cells on collagen-coated gels with source-specific compliant, intermediate and stiff ranges. Compare morphology and neurogenic/myogenic/osteogenic-associated markers after roughly a week, then examine soluble-induction or replating challenges over longer culture periods. Myosin-inhibitor comparisons test a contractility contribution; stiffness calibration and ligand/thickness protocols have their declared source limits.
The source varies the mechanical culture substrate and separately applies soluble-induction/replating or contractility challenges to existing human stromal cells.

Selected morphology/transcripts/proteins vary with the source's substrate conditions, and later challenge responsiveness differs with culture duration. The supported phenotype is not a complete mature cell-function assay or proof that every cellular identity is imposed from above by matrix stiffness.

At a matched initial elastic modulus near 9 kPa and fixed alginate concentration, tune stress-relaxation rate by polymer architecture/crosslink formulation; compare no RGD and source low/high RGD conditions. Culture encapsulated 3T3 fibroblasts and measure day-7 spreading/proliferation, with rheology/compression and seven-day dry-mass controls bounding material stability.
The material design changes relaxation while keeping declared initial modulus, polymer concentration and within-comparison ligand density fixed; ligand-density comparisons are separate factors.

Faster-relaxing adhesive gels permit more spreading/proliferation than slow-relaxing gels in the reported 3T3 preparation. Mechanical remodeling can occur with little measured polymer mass loss, so matrix persistence and fixed geometry are different properties.

Encapsulate clonally derived mouse D1 cells in source gels of about 9 or 17 kPa initial elastic modulus and varied relaxation/RGD conditions. Maintain the specified ascorbate/beta-glycerophosphate/dexamethasone culture environment. Read day-7 lipid/alkaline-phosphatase fate-associated outputs and day-14 collagen/mineral matrix; source ML-7, Y-27632, Rac1 inhibitor and YAP-localization comparisons retain their distinct endpoints.

The source varies initial modulus, relaxation and adhesion in defined D1 cultures receiving the stated differentiation-supporting medium; these factors are not collapsed into one scalar matrix instruction.

At the higher tested initial modulus, faster relaxation enhances osteogenic-associated output and day-14 mineral/collagen deposition; the lower-modulus regime favors different output. Cells form bone-like matrix under these conditions rather than a demonstrated complete bone tissue.

Nuclear YAP spans similar ranges at the two tested moduli despite different adipogenic/osteogenic bias. ML-7 diminishes osteogenic output, whereas the reported ROCK inhibitor can enhance it and Rac1 inhibition lacks the same effect. Shared pathway names therefore do not imply a universal sign or a sufficient fate determinant.

Extract crypts from 5-10-week Lgr5 reporter mice, dissociate or use source ISC cultures and embed in PEG gels. Compare RGD/ECM presentation and shear-modulus conditions with matched expansion medium containing EGF, Noggin, R-spondin, CHIR99021 and valproate; early single-cell culture includes thiazovivin. Score day-4 colony formation and Lgr5, with source YAP knockdown and contractility/adhesion controls.
The source varies adhesive ligands and matrix mechanical properties while supplying the specified soluble expansion regime; plain PEG is not a complete biochemical niche.

RGD-functionalized matrices support source ISC expansion at selected mechanics, whereas plain PEG fails and adhesion/contractility/YAP interventions impair colony formation. This defines culture-stage support rather than a universally optimal material for later organoid differentiation.

Compare the source's stiff PEG-RGD networks containing an MMP-cleavable backbone with corresponding nondegradable cultures under the defined expansion support. Score colony formation together with shape, polarity, Lgr5 and retained organoid-forming capacity after transfer. Keep transcriptome stress/inflammation interpretation bounded by unread Extended Data/raw RNA-seq rather than admitting direct inflammatory tissue pathology.
The source adds a cleavable backbone to the stiff culture network, permitting a different cell-matrix remodeling history under the specified soluble regime.

The source reports enhanced colony formation alongside irregular/depolarized structures, attenuated Lgr5 and reduced retained organoid-forming capacity in degradable stiff matrices. More proliferation or material remodeling therefore does not guarantee preservation of organized tissue potential.

After defined expansion, withdraw CHIR99021/valproate while retaining EGF/Noggin/R-spondin to induce differentiation. Compare matrix softening histories and laminin-based support with static expansion matrices; hybrid PEG chemistry permits gradual softening over days. Score buds and differentiated intestinal cell markers. Transfer and material/adhesion conditions retain their specific preparation rather than a single stiffness-only intervention.
The designed environment supplies an initially supportive expansion stage followed by permissive softening/laminin conditions and the source's differentiation medium change.

Under source-defined dynamic matrix/adhesion conditions, expanded cells produce budded differentiated organoids, whereas static expansion-supporting matrices can buckle or lose the culture during attempted differentiation. A condition optimal for one stage is not automatically compatible with the next.

Use the source's nonmalignant mammary epithelial preparations in collagen/reconstituted-basement-membrane gels. Compare 15 mM ribose-mediated collagen glycation/crosslinking and ErbB2 activation separately and jointly, with corresponding culture controls. Score acinar polarity, junctions and invasion; beta1-integrin, focal-adhesion and PI3K inhibition are separately tested pathway comparisons. Full prior 3D culture timing protocols remain unread.
The source compares unmodified/crosslinked collagen and inactive/active ErbB2 conditions, with distinct pathway-inhibition controls; neither input is replaced by a generic tissue class label.

Crosslinked matrix and ErbB2 activity jointly produce disorganized invasive cultures in the reported comparison; matrix stiffening alone or sustained ErbB2 alone does not reproduce invasion. Specific integrin/PI3K perturbations reduce the combined phenotype, so matrix influence is conditional on the cellular response background.

Compare source MMTV-Neu animals receiving BAPN in drinking water or, in a separate smaller study, a LOX-blocking polyclonal with their controls. Examine mammary collagen/crosslinks, tissue mechanics, lesions and blinded histological grading at source late ages. Keep these spontaneous-oncogene preparations distinct from fibroblast-conditioned fat-pad transplantation and in-vitro ribose cultures.

LOX-directed source preparations show reduced mammary matrix remodeling and less progressed lesions under their oncogenic mouse context. This complements the culture factorial assay without converting it into independent proof that all fibrosis must progress to cancer or that stiffening is a sufficient cause.

Tissue-scale spatial organization is reconstructed through hESC micropatterns, mouse ESC aggregates and epithelial/neural culture preparations, with manipulated geometric/signaling conditions, spatial markers and failed outcomes. Layers, boundaries and axes are distinct measured architectures, not one universal arising. The pattern classification is a project definition; reaction-diffusion, positional information and mechanical interpretations require their own model assumptions. Long-term turnover invariance, all developmental mechanisms and a complete organism are not established by early culture markers.

Organogenesis is represented through explicitly incomplete intestinal epithelial and cerebral organoid models, separating architecture, differentiated markers and bounded neuronal activity. Existing stem-cell descendants can produce organized substructures under engineered matrix, resource and signaling support, with many founder failures and incomplete maturation. These cultures do not demonstrate every organ's multicellular tissue composition, stable lifetime identity, full physiology or an obligatory tissue-to-organ construction law.

Structural integration is reconstructed through zebrafish posterior-axis mechanical measurements and explicit model interpretation, complemented by culture polarity/axis organization. Local adhesion-dependent mechanical integrity, rearrangement and directional growth are measurable; their tissue-scale arrangement differs from a complete all-organ load/transport network. The jamming/continuum account is a separate computational context, and neither one matrix stiffness nor more contractility supplies a universal body-coherence rule.

Repair is reconstructed as distinct outcomes: wound closure, scar persistence, blastema/regrowth, source-specific regeneration restart and cardiomyocyte-derived myocardial replacement. Axolotl phagocyte timing and zebrafish lineage/drug comparisons show that cellular proliferation or closure alone is insufficient and that pre-existing differentiated cells can contribute without compulsory general stem-cell recruitment. Genomic maintenance, stress regulation, matrix remodeling and inflammatory labels are not admitted as a universally necessary weighted bundle.

ECM organization is reconstructed through fibronectin assembly, epithelial basement-membrane-like architecture, injury-associated collagen remodeling and material-state controls. Deposition/abundance, molecular accessibility, fibrillar assembly, bulk mechanics and tissue phenotype are distinct measurements. Synthetic gels provide controlled environmental models; a persistent extracellular architecture can remodel and need not form one globally bounded object. No common matrix composition, universal required antecedent or fixed mechanical threshold is admitted.

Tissue-type organization is represented by contrasting epithelial crypt/cyst architecture, cerebral neural cultures and stromal matrix-producing preparations. Class names summarize arrangements and functions at a chosen descriptive scale; they are not an experimentally closed finite ontology of all multicellular life. Spatial organization, differentiated markers, mature cellular function and whole-tissue physiology remain separate. Continued growth can accompany polarity loss, providing a concrete failure of proliferation alone to establish a canonical tissue architecture.

Stem-cell niches are reconstructed as source-specific relational support and replaceable constraints, principally in intestinal epithelial culture and mouse genetic preparations. Paneth co-culture and exogenous Wnt can assist culture founding, while Atoh1 backgrounds retain long-term stem-cell activity without Paneth cells. Matrix conditions favorable for early expansion can fail later differentiation. Neither an invariant helper-cell list, a universally pre-existing bounded niche object, purely environmental identity nor obligatory niche recruitment in every regeneration is established.

Plasticity/pathology is reconstructed through finite regenerative versus scarred injury outcomes, genetic changes to organoid progenitor organization, matrix-dependent epithelial failure and oncogene/matrix cooperation. Structural alteration can coexist with viability or growth and need not restore physiological function. A persistent scar or invasion phenotype does not by itself identify a dynamical attractor, universal pathological trajectory or measured tissue-wide reconfiguration capacity under all future perturbations. Compensatory hypertrophy and complete disease taxonomy remain outside the admitted cases.

Matrix influence is reconstructed through controlled elasticity/relaxation/adhesion cultures, MDCK polarity orientation and staged intestinal organoid matrices, with conditional oncogene cooperation as a contrary sufficiency example. Effects depend on cell background, medium, mechanical history, material and readout; bulk modulus, YAP localization and matrix abundance are not interchangeable sufficient instructions. Matrix-mediated context is a source-specific operational relation, not a universal downward ontological cause overriding genetic programs or all cellular mechanisms.

P5 eyes receive approximately 0.5 microlitre of 1 microgram/microlitre soluble Flt-1/Fc or receptor-neutralizing reagent; retinas are examined six hours later by whole-mount vascular staining. Reflux makes delivered dose variable. VEGFR1 blockade and control reagents are distinct comparisons.
The intervention changes available VEGF-A or receptor recognition within an already developing retinal plexus; it does not construct endothelium from unorganized material.
At six hours, the tested VEGF trap and VEGFR2 blockade reduce tip-cell filopodia and plexus spreading; VEGFR1 blockade is a pathway-specific negative comparison.

Compare wild-type and VEGF120-only or lens-overexpression preparations, alongside acute VEGF-related ligand additions; confocal morphology and proliferation markers distinguish tip and stalk responses. These interventions differ in genotype, spatial expression and ligand context.
The reported patterning contrasts separate directed tip migration from stalk proliferation: enlarged or proliferating vascular structures need not have normal directed branching.

Retinal dextran perfusion labels lumen up to, but not within, the leading tip cell; proliferation labeling is concentrated behind sampled tips. Morphological sprouting, patent lumen and completed tissue perfusion are distinct.

Tg(epsilon-globin-GFP) Mlc2a-null and littermate embryos collected at 8.5 dpc are staged by somites. Erythroblast tracking and fluorescein-dextran FRAP assess circulation; 8-9-somite plasma measurements are made blind before genotyping.

Mlc2a-null embryos provide a genetic cardiac-contractility perturbation with flow tracked in the connected yolk sac; the vascular consequence is secondary to the whole preparation, not a purified endothelial knockout.
Blood cells can occupy the mutant plexus while moving slowly back and forth, and plasma transport remains measurable. An anatomical connected channel does not guarantee normal circulation.

Polymerized acrylamide sequesters erythroblasts in blood islands; separate acrylamide-only, TEMED-only and untreated controls are retained. Approximately 1-2 hours after polymerization, a low-hematocrit group receives intracardiac 6% hetastarch solution. Embryos develop for 24 hours in roller culture; remodeling/turning are scored blind.

The low-hematocrit manipulation removes most circulating erythroblasts while preserving a comparable measured range of plasma transport, separating circulating-cell contribution from the mere presence of flow.
The hetastarch intervention increases fluid viscosity in the already circulating low-hematocrit preparation while erythroblasts remain confined to blood islands.

Hetastarch restores substantial hierarchical yolk-sac remodeling, area and eNOS signal relative to low hematocrit. This supports a mechanical contribution, without proving universal oxygen dispensability, exact rescue equivalence or a unique shear-sensing mechanism.

P10-P21 cerebellar slices are superfused at 31-35 degrees C with 20% or 95% oxygen; noradrenaline supplies preconstriction, followed by glutamate or parallel-fiber stimulation. EP4 blockade and TTX test selected response components. Nonconstricting capillaries and selected stimulation-induced constrictions are excluded as described in Methods.

The input is a specified glutamate or fiber-stimulation protocol acting on an intact slice with experimentally established vascular tone, rather than isolated direct glutamate action on a single pericyte.

Selected capillaries dilate to stimulation under the reported tone/oxygen conditions; TTX and EP4 perturbations constrain the pathway, while the source does not assign a unique initial responding cell.

Adult NG2-DsRed mice are ventilated and maintained under alpha-chloralose after surgery; physiological blood gases/pressure and temperature are monitored. Electrical infraorbital whisker-pathway stimulation uses 3-Hz, 2- or 15-second trains. Two-photon imaging identifies vessel branch order and local mural-cell position; responding vessels exceed the source 5% diameter criterion.

The reported sensory preparation shows dilation in multiple vessel orders, including early capillary responses near NG2-labeled mural cells; the pericyte attribution is a source interpretation with explicit classification boundaries.

Branch order and labeled soma/process proximity identify tested locations, while anesthesia and the capillary definition differ from the later smooth-muscle-marker comparison. The two studies are not interchangeable quantitative repeats.

NG2-Cre/ChR2-YFP and SMA-mCherry reporters distinguish circumferential smooth-muscle-covered segments from longitudinal pericyte-covered segments. Confocal local line scanning measures diameter; localized two-photon activation limits upstream optical activation in separate velocity measurements. Main Methods specify 4-16-week males and females and awake or ketamine/xylazine states as indicated; not all assay-specific state assignments are reconstructed here.
ChR2 activation is applied at morphologically and SMA-classified vascular sites; small vessel diameter or early branch order alone does not distinguish smooth muscle from capillary pericytes.

The study detects rapid constriction and reduced red-cell velocity in smooth-muscle-covered segments, with no comparable measured response in the specified SMA-negative pericyte segments. The null is bounded to this protocol.

Following acute cranial-window surgery and recovery from anesthesia, NG2-Cre/GCaMP3 mice receive 30 seconds of 5-Hz, 100-ms whisker air puffs. Vascular diameter and neural/mural calcium are measured in smooth-muscle-positive and negative segments.
The awake sensory protocol reports prompt smooth-muscle-associated dilation and calcium decrease; the small delayed capillary change is not treated as direct active pericyte contraction.

Hall and Hill differ in anesthetic state, stimulation, classification and selection. These contrasts leave a mechanistic boundary; shared diameter or branch order does not establish an identical effector population.

Cre-dependent GCaMP6s in VMPO PACAP neurons is monitored by fiber photometry during controlled ambient ramps/steps. Reporter-negative and nearby-population controls distinguish selected optical artifacts and cell populations; slice sensor validation is a separate acquisition.
Controlled ambient temperature changes act on the entire mouse, including peripheral sensors; they are not direct heating of genetically identified isolated neurons.

The selected VMPO population increases calcium activity within seconds during warmth, while tested cold/unrelated stimuli do not show the same activation. Intrinsic sensing and complete afferent circuitry remain unresolved.

Cre-dependent stabilized step-function opsin in VMPO PACAP or BDNF populations is activated by brief blue-light stimulation (2 Hz for 30 seconds, reported 10 mW), with no-opsin controls. Core rectal temperature, tail infrared readings and subcutaneous interscapular temperature are recorded using distinct instruments.
The optogenetic intervention increases excitability of an identified existing preoptic population, with no-opsin illuminated mice as controls.

Core/interscapular cooling and tail warming co-occur under the tested stimulation protocol. This is bounded organ-effector coordination; exact vascular conductance, heat flux and all temperature-feedback paths are unmeasured.

Adult Nos1-Cre mice of both sexes express GCaMP6s in SFO. Hypertonic saline/mannitol, PEG-related hypovolemia or isoproterenol-related hypotension are applied in distinct trials. Losartan and captopril distinguish selected angiotensin-dependent responses. Photometry uses pre-established salt-response and placement exclusions.
The source applies chemically and physiologically distinct perturbations; none is a generic scalar stress input with a common inferred weight.

Specified osmotic and volume/pressure challenges engage SFO Nos1 activity through partly separable angiotensin-dependent and independent routes; no single required upstream hormone covers all tested inputs.

SFO photometry follows drinking after deprivation or salt challenge, with water/saline, empty bottle and oral-cooling comparisons. Plasma osmolality/protein are separately sampled at specified times in matched protocols; they are not simultaneous continuous measures in every imaged animal.
The measured SFO/lick dynamics change well before the separately sampled blood readouts normalize, so behavioral satiation cannot be equated with already restored internal composition.

Hypertonic saline causes a transient early inhibition followed by rebound, separating immediate ingestion-linked signals from delayed information about fluid composition. This is not a permanently fixed homeostatic set point.

After 24-hour water restriction, eArch3.0-expressing SFO Nos1 neurons are inhibited using 532-nm light (10-15 mW) during 15-minute water access; trials with and without illumination are interleaved, followed by light-off observation. Reporter controls and separate feeding comparisons constrain behavioral specificity.
The neural perturbation is imposed during an established dehydrated state and access to water, with interleaved illumination conditions.

Water consumption is suppressed during the defined inhibition period and resumes after light removal. The bounded reversible behavioral output is distinct from proof of completed physiological rehydration.

Optically identified individual SON VPpp neurons are recorded electrophysiologically during water-predicting cues and drinking after water restriction. Separate freely moving photometry trials compare water availability across dehydration and food-induced hyperosmolar contexts. Detailed surgeries, full sex/age allocation and calcium processing reside in unread Supplemental Experimental Procedures.
Identified VPpp firing and separate population recordings decrease following water cues before ingestion; early activity is a predictive neural endpoint rather than observed kidney correction.

The interpretation that rapid VPpp activity changes alter circulating vasopressin and renal water retention relies on additional physiology cited by the authors. This case itself does not measure the complete neural-to-hormone-to-kidney path.

Food-restricted mice receive a familiar food-associated bowl, large or small chow pellets, or matched non-food objects while VPpp population calcium is recorded. The paper contrasts cue period with feeding onset; detailed Supplemental Experimental Procedures remain unread.
Food ingestion and water ingestion have opposite reported activity responses, but only the water condition has a robust pre-ingestive predictive-cue response in the tested training context.
Neuroendocrine neuron activity changes on a seconds timescale. Calling every hormonal process intrinsically slow would conflate signal source, circulation, receptor action and measured endpoint.

Approximately 250-g male Sprague-Dawley rats recover five days after double jugular cannulation. Constant CRH at 0.5, 1.0 or 2.5 micrograms/hour, or saline, is infused from 07:00 to 13:00; corticosterone is sampled every five minutes from 06:00. Doses and time of day are preparation conditions, not universal endocrine thresholds.
The imposed input remains constant over six hours; multiple dose groups test whether peripheral hormone output must simply copy an externally pulsed command.

Corticosterone oscillations can occur under the tested constant lower CRH drive, while larger constant doses damp oscillatory output. A fixed fast-neural/slow-hormonal ordering or requirement for pulsatile hypothalamic input is therefore not assumed.

One protocol samples both hormones every 20 minutes during infusion; a distinct initial-pulse protocol samples every 5 minutes over 25 minutes; separate sacrificed cohorts provide trunk blood at 10-minute intervals over 70 minutes. These are different units and cannot be concatenated into one within-animal high-frequency record.

Apparent coordination depends on assay interval and unit: the short initial series and sacrificed cohorts support ordered hormone onset, whereas the longer 20-minute series lacks resolution for the predicted short phase delay.

The paper displays simulations of a prior feedback model and applies detrending, discrete Fourier transforms and short-time spectra to acquired corticosterone data. The prior model derivation, numerical code and raw hormone traces were not rerun.

The proposed pituitary-adrenal feedback oscillator is compatible with the displayed experiments; neither a fitted diagram nor similar dominant frequencies uniquely identify the complete biological generator.

3617/3617-ChRFP-NF1 cells carry a large MMTV promoter array and fluorescent GR/locus markers. Corticosterone or dexamethasone is applied at 100 nM for 20 minutes followed by 40-minute withdrawal; imaging and FRAP measure locus association. Endogenous-locus ChIP in 3134 cells is a related but separate assay, not an independent whole-organ result.
The experimental input specifies ligand identity, concentration and washout schedule, rather than a generic endocrine signal with one mandatory timescale.

The measured GR-array response follows natural corticosterone withdrawal more rapidly than dexamethasone withdrawal. Nuclear receptor presence does not by itself imply continued productive promoter engagement.

Cells in charcoal-stripped serum receive eight 100-nM corticosterone pulses of 20 minutes separated by 40-minute hormone-free intervals, or constant 100-nM treatment. Nascent intron/exon-spanning qPCR and mature RNA assays are normalized within their reported protocols.
The compared schedules differ in pulse structure and integrated exposure; their biological comparison must preserve both differences.

Selected nascent RNAs track the pulse/washout schedule, while mature transcript accumulation differs from constant treatment. Hormone concentration alone is insufficient to identify this temporal response.

For the Western-blot comparison, 600-nM corticosterone is delivered constantly for 8 hours or in eight 20-minute pulses separated by 40-minute withdrawal. This concentration is distinct from the 100-nM transcription series.
The Fkbp5 protein contrast uses 600 nM and an 8-hour endpoint, so it cannot be silently merged with the 100-nM RNA kinetics as one matched quantitative conversion rate.

Adult 250-300-g rats undergo bilateral adrenalectomy and jugular cannulation, recover 5 days with corticosterone replacement, and have replacement withdrawn 24 hours before testing. Up to three 100-microgram corticosterone-HBC intravenous boluses are given at 0, 60 and 120 minutes; separate terminal cohorts supply plasma and liver.
The systemic input is imposed in adrenalectomized animals whose endogenous adrenal corticosterone source has been removed; it is not a direct test of a complete natural stress circuit.
The source measures transient hepatic GR-associated readouts and Per1 nascent RNA after timed circulating corticosterone replacement, supporting a bounded systemic-signal-to-cell-expression case.

A549 cells are compared in standard RPMI-based medium versus adult bovine serum; reciprocal 3.5-kDa dialysis and cystine addition constrain the nutrient contribution. Eight-hour [U-13C5]glutamine tracing and separate four-day proliferation/CB-839 comparisons have distinct endpoints.
Specified media exchange/dialysis and cystine addition alter an existing cell environment; this is a physical supply constraint rather than a demonstrated goal-directed top-down instruction.
Changing small-molecule conditions changes measured glutamine labeling and inhibitor-sensitive proliferation in A549 cultures, with labeling and growth retained as separate acquisition endpoints.

Control or two SLC7A11-targeting shRNAs are compared with an shRNA-resistant cDNA rescue. Adult bovine serum with or without 208-micromolar cystine is traced for 8 hours with approximately 33% enriched [U-13C5]glutamine; normalized alpha-ketoglutarate labeling quantifies the source contrast.
The genetic intervention and resistant-cDNA rescue are examined in the same declared A549 environmental contrast, avoiding inference of causality solely from cross-cell-line expression correlations.
Knockdown and resistant rescue change the cystine-dependent labeling increment, supporting conditional environmental sensitivity rather than extracellular cystine acting independently of cell state.

Administer 2.4 g/kg cystine by oral gavage and measure plasma cystine by GC-MS at the indicated subsequent times. Figure 5A supplies the plasma time course; a complete group-specific animal manifest and relation to the separately sampled tumor cohort are not reconstructed.
The Figure 5A plasma concentration measurements establish a finite availability response after oral dosing; they do not measure the kinetics of label incorporation within tumors.

Tumor-bearing nu/nu mice receive 2.4 g/kg oral cystine or the comparison condition. Methods specify three 200-microlitre intravenous [U-13C5]glutamine boluses (36.2 mg/mL) at 15-minute intervals, starting 45 minutes after gavage, followed by one terminal plasma/tumor harvest 15 minutes after the last bolus. Results instead state 30 minutes from cystine dosing to tracer administration; this timing conflict remains unresolved. A separate constant-infusion comparison is described as six hours in Results/Figure 1B but 300 minutes in Methods.

The oral intervention changes measured circulating availability in a tumor-bearing mouse, connecting supply manipulation to a tissue sampling context without inventing an organismal optimization objective.

The single terminal tumor harvest has increased fractional labeling after cystine treatment. Faster incorporation and greater eventual steady-state contribution remain alternative explanations; hypothetical Figure 5B curves do not resolve them. Long-term growth, absolute flux and normal-tissue resource allocation are not measured.

Cells are cultured in human-plasma-like medium plus 10% dialyzed heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum, versus RPMI with 5-mM glucose and 10% intact or dialyzed serum. Standard suspension metabolomics and glucose/nitrogen tracing use 24-hour acquisition; the primary AML 8-hour sample is a separate technical-replicate example not pooled here.
The intervention replaces a defined set of extracellular solutes while retaining bovine-serum growth support; it does not recreate a complete human organism or tissue niche.

Multiple metabolic readouts change in cell-dependent ways under HPLM, while measured energy charge is not significantly altered. Reorganization is not equivalent to generalized energetic collapse or one optimal pathway choice.

HPLM derivatives lacking selected solute groups and isolated uric acid are compared, with add-back/dose and 9-methyluric-acid controls. HPLM contains 350-micromolar urate; reported cell metabolomics use 24-hour culture before extraction.
The cell preparation compares urate-containing and urate-depleted media and chemically related control, distinguishing a selected factor from wholesale medium replacement.
Extracellular urate changes selected cellular pyrimidine intermediates; this does not itself demonstrate a complete organismal feedback pathway maintaining the plasma urate concentration.

Purified recombinant wild-type or inactive Y37A/R155A UMPS (20-40 nM) is incubated for 20 minutes at 37 degrees C with 100-micromolar orotate and 300-micromolar PRPP; urate, established inhibitor and related compounds are compared by LC-MS measurement of OMP/UMP products. This assay is separate from living K562 cells.
Urate is changed within the defined recombinant-enzyme/substrate mixture; the inactive mutant and established inhibitor provide controls distinct from tissue physiology.

The purified-enzyme assay reports reduced UMP production with urate, supporting a direct biochemical contribution that does not require neural, inflammatory or organ-level signals in that reaction vessel.

NOMO1 cells in HPLM with or without urate receive 5-fluorouracil or doxorubicin after 24-hour seeding; four-day treatment is assessed by CellTiter-Glo. A distinct 20-micromolar 5-FU 24-hour acquisition measures fluoronucleotides and is not the same viability time course.
The specified urate contrast is crossed with 5-FU versus a distinct drug control rather than assuming that every cytotoxic compound has identical context dependence.
The reported luminescence response changes for 5-FU but not comparably for doxorubicin, providing a counterexample to indiscriminate claims of uniform environmental control of all cellular outputs.

Existing Song2012 evidence supplies a conditional neural-cycle example with incomplete housing-effect rescue; its original scientific records remain unchanged.

Organ homeostasis is reconstructed through distinct mouse thermal-effector, drinking/fluid-signal and rat hormone-dynamics preparations. Defined perturbations and controls expose conditional neural, humoral, circulatory and cellular contributions. Stable capacity is an interpretive vocabulary for existing systems, not proof of one complete feedback architecture, universal operating range or historical generation of every organ. Anticipatory signals can change before blood correction, and stronger constant endocrine drive can change temporal regime rather than merely scale output.

Vascular organization is reconstructed as developmental guidance/remodeling and adult cerebral response cases with distinct scales and readouts. Retinal VEGF patterning can dissociate directed growth from proliferation; yolk-sac viscosity rescue distinguishes mechanical flow contributions from circulating erythroblast presence; adult mural-cell attribution remains preparation-dependent and contested. A branching anatomical network, patent lumen, blood-cell presence, transport rate, exchange and organ oxygenation are separate properties.

Neural physiological coordination is reconstructed through genetically targeted mouse thermoregulatory and thirst circuits plus distinct cerebral vascular response assays. Neural perturbations can alter multiple bounded effectors or reversibly change drinking. Existing differentiated circuits are the bearers; the data do not construct a full nervous system, prove every reflex arc or pathfinding mechanism, or require higher cognition. Neural, endocrine and behavioral endpoints can all act rapidly, so a universal fast-neural/slow-hormone split is excluded.

Endocrine organization is reconstructed using rat CRH-pituitary-adrenal hormone dynamics, timed circulating corticosterone-to-liver transcription and measured mouse vasopressin-neuron anticipation. Glands, hormone concentrations, target machinery and feedback models are kept distinct from their measured outputs. Dose and exposure history can change temporal regime; endocrine action is not intrinsically one slow scalar channel. Formation of all glands and control of every growth, reproductive, stress and metabolic program are not inferred from these selected axes.

Neuroendocrine integration is reconstructed as source-bound relationships between identified neural populations, systemic cues and hormone dynamics. Mouse VPpp activity predicts selected ingestive consequences; rat pituitary-adrenal output can oscillate under constant CRH drive, and timed glucocorticoid replacement changes hepatic transcription. These are distinct preparations, not one experimentally closed bidirectional whole-organism loop. The pattern concept organizes comparisons without inventing new physical links between different species or studies.

Trophic metabolic regulation is reconstructed through actual extracellular nutrient/media changes, a matched xCT genetic contrast and an acute systemic cystine-to-xenograft labeling experiment. These establish conditional supply/transport/metabolism relationships, alongside a direct cell-free urate/UMPS contribution and drug-specific response limits. They do not prove purposive downward optimization, universal dependence on inflammatory context or that cell isolation reproduces an entire physiological regulatory envelope. Hormonal gene responses are a separate source context, not an unmeasured metabolic flux.

Neuroendocrine expression influence is reconstructed with ligand-dependent GR promoter dynamics, separate pulsed/constant cell RNA and protein assays, and a systemic corticosterone-to-rat-liver transcription experiment. Hormone identity, dose, cumulative exposure, receptor occupancy, nascent RNA, mature RNA and protein are not interchangeable. The existing physiological source architecture provides context, while an unmeasured direct neural-to-chromatin path, heritable epigenetic rewrite, all tissue programs and a universal stable regulatory envelope remain unestablished.

The former has bidirectional stimulation/inhibition contrasts and incomplete housing-effect rescue; the latter separates loss of Gli1 identity from retained telogen quiescence, one regeneration cycle and acute wound closure, while later labeled-lineage retention falls. These are selected target compartments with different outputs, not universal neural control of all division or a measured common proliferative threshold.

A once-daily RTB101 group had fewer laboratory-confirmed RTIs in the prespecified unadjusted analysis, while the multiplicity-controlled fixed-sequence procedure stopped after the first comparison failed. The exploratory signal is not a blanket confirmatory gain in immune function.
