Seven men and one protan carrier pass the source's color-vision tests; some subjects were selected for extreme ratios.

Human local cone-class composition varies substantially despite normal scores on the named color-vision tests; a geometrically packed mosaic does not imply a fixed repeating L/M label lattice or a universal class ratio.

Compare observed inter-cone separations against 100 random-label simulations and the source's cumulative-histogram statistics. Interpret S-cone and L/M-cone results with the official corrected Figures 6 and 9, preserving classification uncertainty and the unread supplementary optical-blur analysis.

The source separates S-cone spatial regularity from broadly irregular L/M labeling; apparent local clumping can depend on optical identification error. These null comparisons do not measure a developmental sorting mechanism.

Compare the local adaptive-optics classifications with flicker-photometric ERG estimates using an approximately 70 degree retinal field, 31.25 Hz alternating lights and source pigment/lens corrections. The same eight current observers provide the fitted comparison; older comparison points and a broader historical histogram are separate datasets.

The local optical and wide-field ERG estimates correlate, but their fitted relation is not unit slope; the proposed greater M-cone contribution is an interpretation under the spectral-weighting model rather than a direct measurement of every cone's gain.

Trace whole-eye projections to the superior colliculus in adult and P2 mouse preparations, keeping the source genotype groups and ages separate. Quantify spatial fluorescence after background subtraction and the declared anatomical region selection; adult groups contain 4 WT, 7 heterozygous and 8 null mice, whereas P2 compares 3 heterozygous with 2 null mice.

Math5-null projections are concentrated in an anteromedial collicular region rather than filling the target like the source controls. This is a genotype-dependent projection result, not direct proof that cell number alone or a unique competition law determines every map.
Compare the source WT/heterozygous and Math5-null developmental preparations rather than imposing an abstract cell-count threshold.

Inject 0.2-1 microlitre CTB-555 or CTB-488 at focal collicular sites in P8-P10 mice and inspect the contralateral retinal flat mount two days later. Compare retinal origins of labeled cells for the source control and Math5-null preparations.

A focal collicular injection labels a relatively clustered retinal origin in controls but a dispersed origin in the null preparation; compressed target coverage is distinct from preservation of detailed retinal-to-target order.

Compare the source's competition, dual-gradient and servomechanism alternatives across two axes under supplied label/activity assumptions and reduced modeled input. Treat the published simulations and qualitative comparison as source results; detailed SI parameterization and optimization are not reconstructed.

The modeled competition account reproduces important aspects of reduced-input target compression, while discrepancies and alternative weak influences remain; successful restricted comparison does not uniquely identify a universal topographic construction mechanism.

In DRD4-GFP, TRHR-GFP and selected non-GFP recordings from P14-P88 mice, establish tuning using 3 second gratings in 12 directions repeated 3-5 times. Present the named preferred-null protocol, 40 seconds in each direction, and retest; keep alternative protocols, selected sharp-tuning criteria and finite follow-up separate.

The preferred-null protocol produces reversed, ambiguous and stable cells in the same reported comparison: 9, 9 and 6 of 24, respectively. Thus selected circuit responses can change with recent stimulation even though the anatomical substrate is supplied.
Apply the source's preferred-null adaptation protocol to previously characterized On-Off direction-selective cells.

Use the source 5-20 micromolar L-AP4 comparison with spot and grating tests, then apply the preferred-null adaptation protocol. Preserve the distinction between the 24-cell initial blockade characterization and the 21 adapting cells, of which 6 cease responding and 15 remain for the stated post-adaptation comparison.

On-pathway blockade changes response classes and does not eliminate every adaptation-associated reversal; loss of responsiveness and recovered On components constrain a simple independent-channel interpretation.

Express PSAM-GlyR through source intravitreal AAV in P6-P8 ChAT-Cre mice and assay the isolated adult retinal preparation. Apply 20 micromolar PSEM89S for at least 15 minutes and measure direction-selective calcium responses to moving UV bars before, during and after ligand exposure; keep the main-text WT ligand control separate from the unread supplementary evidence.

Ligand activation of the targeted chloride conductance reduces direction selectivity, and washout increases it again. The post-washout mean remains below the starting mean; this is finite recovery of a defined calcium response, not proof of exact restoration or universal direction-selective circuitry.
Activate the expressed PSAM conductance with PSEM89S in the declared retinal calcium-imaging preparation.

In isolated P21-P40 retinal preparations, estimate excitatory and inhibitory conductances from five sweeps at four holding potentials. Compare 2 second spot responses before and after the main grating sequence, including its 40 second nasal and temporal segments; retain dorsal/ventral cone activation and spectral comparisons as distinct controls.

Adapted On-starburst cells can lose onset excitation and gain offset excitation. The appearance of the offset component depends on cone activation in the source's spectral/retinal-location comparisons; one fixed wiring diagram is insufficient to specify these responses.

Use the reported rectified-sinusoid excitatory/inhibitory input model with excitation held fixed while inhibitory phase changes. The source calculates direction selectivity from 100 stochastic spike trains for the preferred/null comparison; illustrative traces and biological recordings remain separate.

A conditional phase shift can reverse the modeled directional index. This establishes a possible implementation under the source assumptions rather than a unique experimentally identified cause of biological reversal.

Use flat-mounted retinas from overnight dark-adapted 6-8 week C57/BL6 mice, warmed oxygenated Ames perfusion and repeated spatially uniform 470 nm Gaussian flicker with 0-60 Hz bandwidth and a source mean near 2.5 photoisomerizations per rod per second. Record spikes cell-attached and distinguish burst-first-spike and spike-distance analyses.

The recorded spike responses are temporally more precise than the slow rod response alone suggests, while precision and excitation/inhibition differ across the named cell classes. The burst-first-spike metric samples fewer than five percent of spikes; the source distance-based comparison covers more than 85 percent under its pairing rule.

Measure light-evoked excitatory/inhibitory waveforms and compare repeated fixed or averaged waveform pairs with randomly selected trial-varying pairs during somatic conductance clamp. Block AMPA/kainate, NMDA and GABA/glycine input with the source NBQX, MK-801 and high-concentration strychnine conditions. Representative waveforms come from one example cell per class; the current feedback is computed at 10 kHz.

Fixed injected inputs yield more precise spikes than natural light responses, while trial-varying measured inputs recover much of the observed variability. Under these conditions, variable network input is an important timing limitation; this does not show that intrinsic noise is universally absent.
Change the trial-to-trial waveform variation while retaining the source conductance-clamp and synaptic-blocker conditions.

Record ganglion spikes with a multielectrode array in oxygenated Ringer's solution. Repeat spatially uniform Gaussian flicker updated every 30 ms at the reported photopic mean, using 100 repeats of 20 seconds or 30 repeats of 800 seconds. For the fast-OFF contrast comparison, retain the changing cell/retina membership of the six contrast groups rather than treating all contrasts as paired measurements in one population.

Timing precision depends on contrast and cell class; fast-OFF jitter increases as contrast falls, and its Fano factor can rise above one at low contrast. The source therefore does not support uniformly low-noise or uniformly sub-Poisson output from every ganglion cell under every input.
Change the source flicker contrast in the specified salamander fast-OFF comparisons, retaining unequal sample membership and event-analysis rules.

Use the same reported repeated-flicker framework but preserve the rabbit preparation, Ames medium at 37 degrees Celsius and its separate cell sample. The source report contains 45 cells from two rabbit retinas; the Figure 3 9-percent-contrast histogram uses 30 cells from two retinas rather than the entire recorded sample.

Rabbit cells exhibit diverse response patterns and sparseness under the source stimulus; some are not very sparse and some have count Fano factor above one. The source does not establish a single invariant mammalian spike symbol or communication reliability law.

Apply the reported heuristic entropy comparison to event-first-spike timing and count distributions from the repeated-flicker recordings. Retain the Gaussian approximation, independence assumptions and separate treatment of event-time and count information; the source notes deviations from those assumptions.

Under the source's event and ensemble definitions, estimated timing information exceeds count information in the illustrated comparisons; this is an analytical interpretation of shared recordings, not direct evidence that the brain uses the full estimate or that multiplexing is optimal.

The official Hofer correction replaces a duplicated Figure 6 with the corrected S-cone comparison and also prints the correct Figure 9 for L/M-cone comparisons. They remain analyses of the original observations rather than new data.

A supplied ocular optical interface is described through whole-eye wavefront measurement, anterior-boundary manipulation and a separate component model. These constrain image-forming optics without establishing organogenesis, every enabling tissue function or an active alignment controller.

The reviewed optical measurements do not reconstruct transparency maintenance, pupil-control dynamics, accommodation, developmental assembly, a unique compensation mechanism or a complete spectral-to-neural transfer function.

Retinal sampling is separated into local photoreceptor-class geometry, measurement/classification uncertainty and an independently prepared retinal-to-collicular projection. A registered sampling representation, anatomical topography and visual performance are different claims.

Whole-field receptor-density/anisotropy maps, matched local convergence ratios, perceptual acuity and a unique developmental mechanism are not jointly measured in these preparations. Local adult mosaics and developing mouse central projections cannot be combined into one complete visual map.

Circuit preprocessing is reconstructed through reversible surround/opponency interventions already admitted in primate tissue and new mouse direction/polarity experiments. Stimulus history, cell class, spectral access, readout and model assumptions constrain which transformation is actually supported.

The reviewed cases do not identify every preprocessing mechanism, quantify a universal noise/redundancy reduction or establish that anatomy uniquely fixes a stable filter. The proposed phase/crossover implementation and ecological downstream use remain discriminating-test obligations.

Retinal spike encoding is described by measured input-dependent spike timing/counts and separate analytical interpretations. Natural synaptic input, somatic injection, intrinsic ganglion photoreception, downstream relay and hypothetical code use retain their distinct preparations.

The admitted retinal measurements do not establish a universal analog-to-digital threshold law, noise-resistant communication guarantee, optimal multiplexing code or complete downstream use of inferred information. Supplied cells and measured conductances are not a de novo spike-generator construction.

Neural network formation is reconstructed through anatomical developmental comparisons in different C. elegans individuals and an axon-contact coculture intervention. Similar neurite geometry can coexist with changing chemical connectivity, while neuroligin-expressing nonneuronal contacts can induce local presynaptic differentiation. These are different species/preparations and different endpoints; neither establishes a complete persistent network, its physiological coupling weights, a universal modular architecture or a developmental hierarchy. A structural connection, local differentiation and measured effective propagation remain distinct evidence types.

Activity-dependent plasticity is represented by persistent dentate population-response changes after perforant-path conditioning and NMDA-antagonist sensitivity of CA1 potentiation induction. Behavioral force-field adaptation and aftereffects provide a separate learning-related trajectory, without a directly measured bridge to those hippocampal synapses. Potentiation induction, basal transmission, excitability, behavioral retention and structural remodeling are not interchangeable. The general claim that synaptic history implements learning remains a hypothesis requiring task-specific causal tests.

Rhythmic organization is reconstructed through fast-spiking-cell activation that amplifies local gamma and a phase-sensitive whisker-response assay in barrel cortex. Local field potential, sorted unit response and stimulation timing remain distinct observables. The results support a preparation-bound intervention on temporal organization; they do not establish every frequency band, cross-frequency coupling, whole-brain synchrony, semantic code or universal prerequisite for cognition.

Decision making is reconstructed through task-specific macaque motion choices, reaction times, spatial free choices and perturbation time courses. LIP stimulation alters choices and response times, while one verified LIP-silencing design shows no detected motion deficit despite strong decision-related correlations; a different design reports early bias with attenuation. MT silencing and spatial control tasks give further contrasts. Evidence accumulation, competitive thresholds and compensation are candidate explanations, not a uniquely identified universal cognitive architecture.

Sensory integration is represented by a visual-haptic height-discrimination experiment in four adult observers. Manipulated visual reliability and small cue discrepancies alter combined judgments and thresholds in a way resembling a declared maximum-likelihood comparison. The model assumes aligned cues, independent Gaussian estimator noise and a uniform prior. This is bounded behavioral cue combination, not a directly identified neural implementation, every multisensory operation or proof of universally optimal or consciously unified perception.

Motor control is reconstructed through force-dependent hand-localization judgments, force-field reaching adaptation and field-removal aftereffects. The localization experiment contrasts assistive, resistive and null forces during constrained movement without arm vision; its tuned state-estimator account remains separate from the measured biases. Reaching adaptation supplies a different behavioral preparation with only abstract-level inherited reading. These examples do not identify one neural Kalman filter, all feedback/gain operations or a complete distributed movement-control circuit.

Affective processing is represented by projection-specific changes in mouse open-arm/center exploration under distinct BLA-to-CeA activation and inhibition preparations. Terminal activation and direct BLA somatic activation produce contrasting exploration outcomes; inhibition uses a separate low-stress bilateral preparation. These assays support bounded circuit effects on behavioral proxies. They do not measure subjective feeling, a single system-wide evaluative property or simultaneous control of valence, salience, cognition, perception, learning and motor readiness.

Neuromodulation is reconstructed through optogenetic LC manipulations and EEG/EMG-defined mouse sleep/wake endpoints. Brief activation promotes awakening; prolonged active-period inhibition reduces wake duration but leaves awakenings possible; inactive-period inhibition has no detected duration effect. These schedule- and state-dependent results support a particular noradrenergic circuit contribution. They do not establish a spatially uniform global transmitter state, identical effects of dopamine/serotonin/acetylcholine or unchanged anatomical topology.

Collective dynamics are reconstructed through sampled LFP event cascades in cortical cultures, separate drug-activated acute slices and the distributional response to culture picrotoxin. Event threshold, sampling and binning define an avalanche; phase synchronization and criticality at a specified transition require additional observables. Recovery of an event-size distribution after washout supports a bounded reversible perturbation. Scale-like statistics alone do not prove self-organized criticality, optimal information processing or a necessary organizational condition for cognition.

Conscious experience remains an explicitly unresolved theoretical scope. IIT, GNWT and conceptual global-workspace architecture are distinct versioned proposals, not one combined physiological rule. The COGITATE visual-task data provide region/feature/modality-dependent decoding, duration-related activity and differing preregistered phase versus exploratory amplitude connectivity results. These recordings neither causally generate experience nor measure Phi or establish a unique necessary integration threshold. Reportable access, neural content readout and subjective experience remain distinct explanatory targets.

Sleep/wake regulation is reconstructed through EEG/EMG-defined mouse transition and duration endpoints under distinct Hcrt and LC interventions. Hcrt stimulation shortens post-stimulation wake latency under specified trains, with low-frequency and total-duration nulls and receptor-blockade contrasts. LC activation and inhibition have schedule- and circadian-period-dependent effects. Transition probability/latency, wake duration and sleep function are separate; two-process and synaptic-homeostasis accounts remain interpretations rather than experimentally closed universal state-control laws.

Functional ensembles are reconstructed as operational calcium co-activation groups in a learned visual licking task. Nonselective stimulation can disrupt, and selected pattern-completion stimulation can improve, task-associated ensemble recruitment and measured performance, while non-pattern-completion controls do not show the same improvement. Gray-screen behavioral comparisons condition on a small successful-recall subset. These results support task- and selection-specific participation; they do not establish fixed anatomical modules, universal division of labor, minimum functional units or the subjective percept caused by stimulation.

Connectomic processing is reconstructed through targeted neural stimulation and downstream calcium responses in immobilized C. elegans. AVJR-to-AVDR and AVER-to-AVAR increases and a SAADL-to-OLLR decrease are preparation-bound effective responses, potentially including indirect routes. An anatomical connectome, a perturbation-response atlas, a statistical dependency and a Shannon communication model are distinct objects. The evidence does not identify every path, hub operation, recurrent computation, semantic content or a universal mapping from wiring to function.

Thalamic visual transfer is reconstructed through paired-spike retinal efficacy and separate corticogeniculate perturbation results. Closely spaced retinal spikes differ in conditional transfer efficacy; removing layer-6 cortical input can increase or decrease dLGN responses depending on cell and contrast, while driving input reduces evoked counts in the read source. The feedback preparation uses adult GN220 Ntsr1-Cre mice during acute isoflurane-anesthetized recordings, with concentration adjusted around 1.2% using cortical LFP state. These observations distinguish retinal transmission from cortical feedback and exclude one universal positive-gain sign. They do not identify the transfer's unique cellular mechanism or jointly establish awake attention, neuromodulation, noise suppression and oscillatory routing.

Visual feature organization is reconstructed through a primate striate-cortex column report, rat V1 orientation selectivity without discernible local orientation organization and a separate cat area-18 comparison. Feature selectivity and spatial maps are distinct; a selective population need not display a locally ordered map at the sampled scale. Functionally assigned thalamocortical connections favor matching contrast sign and receptive-field alignment, but correlation-based assignment does not establish map development. The original 1962 cat reference and 1968 monkey study retain their distinct identities.

Top-down visual modulation is reconstructed through sub-saccadic-threshold FEF stimulation and V4 response changes, complemented by a separate corticogeniculate feedback assay. Retinotopically corresponding FEF stimulation enhances responses while noncorresponding stimulation can suppress them, with dependence on stimulus configuration. This supports a bounded intervention on visual response gain. Predictive coding, expectation comparison, error signals and iterative internal-world-model control remain explicit interpretations requiring task-matched alternatives; top-down modulation and prediction are not synonymous measurements.

Glial regulation is a family of source-specific interactions involving astrocytic ionic/uptake currents, lactate-related retention effects, myelin/conduction associations, developmental microglial engulfment, adult process responses and purinergic perturbations. These are not one homogeneous stabilizing property. Larval radial-astrocyte feedback and behavior oppose an absolute exclusion of glia from task-related information processing. Positive, negative and null outcomes retain cell class, age, region, manipulation and endpoint identity; no all-glia algorithm or universal regulatory architecture is admitted.

Keep electrical uptake proxies, astrocyte calcium, extracellular glutamate sensors, myelin anatomy, compound conduction, engulfed material, tissue fluorescence, dialysate concentration and behavior separate. Distinguish developmental deletion, adult perturbation, acute stimulation and anatomical observation. A morphological contact or colocalization is not direct inhibitory transmission; a partial behavioral effect is not an all-glia information-processing law.

The reconstructed scope separates acute ECS-associated dentate accessibility/RNA responses, maternal-environment and broad TSA-associated hippocampal molecular/endocrine contrasts, and five-day activity-tagged hippocampal population profiles. These sources support finite activity/environment-responsive regulation with distinct molecular assays. They do not establish one sustained abstract neural state, a unique chromatin-to-behavior chain, permanent reprogramming, inherited memory or a substrate-independent downward causal law.

Separate environmental manipulation, neural stimulation, reporter-based selection and molecular perturbation. Accessibility, DNA modification, histone association, contact frequency, RNA abundance, protein puncta and endocrine/behavioral responses retain different units and cohorts. Population overlaps through 24 hours or five days are not same-cell trajectories; a chromatin-associated model is not an experimentally identified unique generative mechanism.

Neuroimmune interactions are represented by distinct mouse immune-to-neural and neural-to-circulating-cytokine assays, including LPS/cytokine challenges, vagotomy, cNST/nodose targeting and endpoint-specific controls. Reciprocal influences are supported in bounded preparations, while the complete descending route, immune effector cells and direct cytokine-receptor mediation remain unresolved. Reduced inflammation, endotoxin survival and control of live infection are different outcomes: improved endotoxin survival cannot override increased Salmonella tissue burden under another neural-activation protocol.

Distinguish FOS, population photometry, single-cell calcium, transcript clusters, retrograde tracing, circulating cytokines, corticosterone, endotoxin survival and live-infection colony counts. Vagotomy, chemogenetic population activation, an immune challenge and direct cytokine delivery are different interventions. Reciprocal findings across assays constrain a candidate circuit; they do not identify a complete matched feedback path or a universal benefit of inflammation suppression.

The reconstructed vascular scope concerns activity-associated vascular responses, capillary potassium-sensitive signaling and arterial connexin-dependent response propagation. It separates isolated-cell current, ex vivo diameter/membrane potential, in vivo RBC flux, relative perfusion and optical HbT-related signals. Neural-to-vascular segments are experimentally constrained, but the physiological potassium source, segment transitions, full signal carrier and inverse neural readout remain unresolved. The original immune-topic short/long descriptions do not define vascular coupling; their immune assertions are not admitted as vascular findings.

Keep capillary endothelial patch-clamp current, upstream smooth-muscle voltage, pressurized diameter, RBC flux, relative laser-Doppler perfusion, retinal tracer spread, aortic electrical coupling and cortical HbT-related optical response as separate preparations and observables. Inverse onset-time/distance fits describe optical response spread, not directly recorded cerebral electrical conduction. Stimulation and response profiles constrain a candidate route without uniquely constructing it or proving bidirectional neural-immune regulation.

Adult neuron production and remodeling of existing circuits are distinct source-scoped processes. Selected mouse birth-label, electrophysiological and optogenetic assays support maturation and circuit participation in restricted dentate preparations; task, running, niche and injury effects concern separate stages and cohorts. Primate histology, human BrdU, radiocarbon models and transcript-based annotation have different inferential reach. Mature-spine remodeling need not entail neuron birth, normal adult neurogenesis need not follow injury, and no universal learning prerequisite, human cognitive mechanism or uniquely minimal construction rule is established.

Distinguish cell-cycle entry, birth-label retention, neuronal/glial markers, static morphology, clonal ancestry, synaptic contact, recorded input/output, mature-neuron spine turnover and behavioral performance. Each stage uses its own age and exposure window. Human transcript annotation, BrdU colabeling and radiocarbon model fits do not substitute for each other or for functional lineage tracing; endpoint population balance is not proof of feedback control or individual asymmetric division.

Use tourniquet-induced ischemic arm pain and the participant's time to intolerable pain. Compare repeated no-treatment days, hidden naloxone, an openly administered saline injection described as an analgesic and an openly administered naloxone injection given the same analgesic description. Retain separate groups and pre/post no-treatment days; the 229 analyzed people across twelve groups are not 229 independent replications of each contrast.

The experimental input combines analgesic verbal framing with an open injection, against no-treatment baseline and a hidden-naloxone control. Naloxone is an active antagonist used to test the framing-associated response, not an inert placebo ingredient.

Analgesic-described saline increases tourniquet pain-tolerance duration; the corresponding naloxone condition does not retain that increase. Hidden naloxone alone gives no significant baseline change. This supports an opioid-receptor contribution to the tested response without directly measuring opioid release or proving a single universal placebo mechanism.

Pair analgesic-described morphine or ketorolac with the pain test on two days. On the test day substitute saline or naloxone and describe the injection either as the earlier analgesic or as a neutral antibiotic. Keep eight conditioning groups, their prior drugs, verbal cues and pre/post untreated days separate.

The source contrasts morphine versus ketorolac preconditioning, analgesic versus antibiotic test descriptions and saline versus naloxone substitution. These are distinct group-level interventions rather than one pooled expectancy dose.

Morphine-conditioned tolerance responses are naloxone-sensitive under either tested description. Ketorolac-conditioned responses with analgesic cues are partly naloxone-sensitive; under antibiotic description the source reports a residual naloxone-insensitive response. The ketorolac difference between descriptions is not conventionally significant in the reported comparison, so no measured additive expectation effect is inferred there.

Compare untreated repeated pain tests with analgesic or hyperalgesic descriptions of saline. In separate groups give ketorolac for two conditioning days and saline on the next test day with analgesic versus opposite hyperalgesic instructions. Measure time from the last standardized hand squeeze until the participant stops because pain is intolerable.

Saline is described as analgesic or pain-increasing, either without new preconditioning or after the same two-day ketorolac procedure. Untreated days and a no-treatment group constrain change unrelated to the test description.

Analgesic suggestions increase and hyperalgesic suggestions decrease measured tolerance in their tested groups. After ketorolac preconditioning, the opposite hyperalgesic description prevents the usual positive test-day response and yields lower tolerance. This does not show that verbal expectation controls every physiological endpoint.

Keep the active stimulation setting unchanged on three ordered-varied test days. Compare no new instruction with a sham switch-off description and a sham intensity-increase description. Measure right-hand directional-choice movement velocity immediately before and thirty minutes after instructions, averaging fifteen reaches per test; earlier actual switch-off observations are historical conditioning context, not concurrent randomized active-stimulation controls.
Patients receive no new instruction, a claimed switch-off or a claimed intensity increase while their subthalamic stimulation actually remains on at the same setting.

The sham switch-off description is followed by slower instrumented hand movement, whereas the sham-increase and no-treatment pre/post comparisons are nonsignificant. The source supports instruction-sensitive behavior under ongoing treatment; it does not demonstrate that the positive description improves movement beyond baseline.

GH groups separately receive suggested increase/decrease, with or without two previous days of subcutaneous sumatriptan. Compare serial blood measurements before and through seventy-five minutes after the test injection, with the source's untreated serial-sampling group. The ninety-five-person hormone sample is distributed over nine groups; GH and cortisol intervention groups are not identical participant cohorts.
The source contrasts saline test instructions in opposite directions, with versus without two previous sumatriptan exposures, retaining separate untreated sampling controls.

Opposite verbal suggestions without sumatriptan preconditioning produce no significant reported GH concentration change in this sampling window. This is a scoped null with finite group size, not proof of exact equality or universal incapacity.
Following sumatriptan conditioning, test-day saline is associated with increased GH despite either direction of verbal suggestion.

Cortisol groups separately receive suggested decrease/increase, with or without two previous days of subcutaneous sumatriptan. Compare serial blood measurements before and through seventy-five minutes after the test injection, with the source's untreated serial-sampling group. The ninety-five-person hormone sample is distributed over nine groups; GH and cortisol intervention groups are not identical participant cohorts.
The source contrasts saline test instructions in opposite directions, with versus without two previous sumatriptan exposures, retaining separate untreated sampling controls.

Opposite verbal suggestions without sumatriptan preconditioning produce no significant reported cortisol concentration change in this sampling window. This is a scoped null with finite group size, not proof of exact equality or universal incapacity.
Following sumatriptan conditioning, test-day saline is associated with decreased cortisol despite either direction of verbal suggestion.

At twelve visits compare randomized within-block albuterol inhaler, placebo inhaler, sham acupuncture and no intervention, each repeated in three blocks. Measure baseline and twenty-minute-interval spirometry for two hours and summarize maximum FEV1 improvement. Participants are screened for at least twelve-percent reversibility to open albuterol; results do not characterize all asthma patients.
The same crossover design separates active bronchodilator exposure from placebo inhaler, sham acupuncture and a no-intervention visit, retaining their unequal blinding conditions.

Measured maximum FEV1 improves substantially more with albuterol; the placebo inhaler and sham-acupuncture contrasts against no intervention are nonsignificant. Improvement relative to each visit's baseline alone therefore does not identify a placebo-caused bronchodilator effect.

Collect perceived symptom improvement on an improvement-only zero-to-ten visual scale after each condition in the twelve-visit crossover. Rescaling these scores as percentages does not transform them into measured percent FEV1. Keep placebo-versus-no-intervention symptom contrasts separate from the same participants' spirometric endpoint.
The source compares improvement-only symptom reports after active inhaler, inactive inhaler, sham acupuncture and no intervention in the same repeated-visit design.

Participants report greater improvement after either sham intervention than after no intervention. The active-versus-placebo report contrast is nonsignificant despite the separate active-drug spirometric benefit. Reported relief and measured airway caliber must not be merged, and nonsignificance does not prove equal subjective experience.

Pair four oral cyclosporine exposures with a novel drink during acquisition, then after washout pair the drink with placebo capsules on four evocation occasions. The control cohort receives placebo throughout. Compare baseline, active-drug, washout and final blood draws; stimulate isolated PBMC with anti-CD3 for twenty-four hours and quantify culture-supernatant IL-2.
Repeated drink/placebo evocation after cyclosporine versus placebo-only acquisition
Previously published experiment-A observations, re-expressed as baseline-relative change here, show lower stimulated IL-2 output after conditioned evocation than in the source control.

Use the same acquisition drug/drink pairing but one drink/placebo evocation on day ten, with a corresponding placebo-only acquisition control. Sample blood two hours later and measure anti-CD3-stimulated PBMC culture IL-2. Keep this cohort and its final evocation-to-sampling interval distinct from experiment A.
Single drink/placebo evocation after cyclosporine versus placebo-only acquisition
A single evocation produces no significant IL-2 suppression relative to its own control in the reported comparison.

Assign declared probabilities of twenty-five, fifty, seventy-five or one hundred percent of receiving cyclosporine, with eight or nine participants per group. All capsules are placebo and are taken four times across three days; no cyclosporine conditioning is performed. Compare pre/post anti-CD3-stimulated PBMC supernatant IL-2 by group and time.

The all-placebo, unconditioned probability groups show no significant reported suppression pattern in stimulated supernatant IL-2. This does not identify a universal cognitive/immune barrier or supply a zero-expectation control.

Use blood before and after the same declared-probability capsule procedure, but activate cells with PMA/ionomycin and brefeldin A and quantify the percentage of intracellular IL-2-positive CD4 T cells by flow cytometry. This is a different stimulation/readout from anti-CD3 culture-supernatant concentration, reusing participants rather than independently replicating them.

The separate intracellular CD4-cell assay also gives nonsignificant reported group and interaction results. Concordant nulls remain dependent endpoints of the same finite expectation experiment, not proof of precise equality or impossibility.

A placebo effect requires a specified intervention and comparator. Improvement within a placebo arm can include time course, regression, repeated measurement and report effects. Symptom reports, task behavior, objective peripheral assays and pathophysiology are different observables; changing one does not establish change in all others.

Wager and Atlas propose interacting conceptual processes, learned associations and affective/motivational states with outcome-dependent neurophysiological mediation. This is a candidate framework, not a measured single route from higher-order meaning to every autonomic, endocrine, immune and symptom endpoint.

Benedetti and colleagues interpret instruction-sensitive pain/motor responses and conditioning-sensitive hormone responses in terms of conscious versus unconscious processes. The observed endpoint contrast motivates this interpretation but does not establish a universal boundary between classes of physiological functions.

Working memory is represented by specified delayed-task maintenance and interference/priority readouts, with storage, rehearsal, binding, control and updating as distinct functional constructs. Macaque PF recordings and human fMRI/TMS-EEG/behavior contexts support bounded observations without identifying a unique continuous-firing or silent-synaptic mechanism. Guided activation, episodic buffering and adaptive gating remain attributed proposals. A process classification does not establish a complete executive architecture, universal time window or mandatory cognitive-control/plasticity/rhythm construction chain.

Symbolic representation is a family of operational definitions and hypotheses concerning reference, composition, transfer and internal use beyond a present stimulus. Sequence continuation, eye movements, fMRI/MEG and neural-network embedding analyses provide distinct bounded tests; they do not jointly demonstrate a complete neural language of thought or one necessary physical construction. Fixed-language description costs, proposed vector binding, program induction and conceptual bootstrapping remain separate from measured circuits, universal minimum resources and a general-purpose stable cognitive capacity.

Social recognition, action observation, self-other distinction, affect sharing, mental-state attribution and helping are distinct constructs and outcomes. Macaque F5 recordings, clinical human action units, cued partner-pain fMRI and clinical pain-picture iEEG/ratings support their own sampled responses, not one necessary mirror/empathy circuit. Proposed shared representations and shared-manifold/neurodynamic mechanisms remain hypotheses, with instrument identity, spatial-overlap, statistical-directionality and clinical-sampling boundaries explicit.

Treatment descriptions, conditioning history and contextual procedures can change specific pain-tolerance, motor, hormone, immune-cell or symptom-report outcomes in existing participants. These endpoints have different mechanisms and controls: opioid-sensitive versus opioid-insensitive conditioned pain, nocebo slowing without proven positive motor gain, conditioned hormone/IL-2 changes with suggestion-only nulls, and perceived asthma relief without demonstrated sham bronchodilation. This is a bounded family of psychophysiological/context effects, not a universal downward-causation law, belief-only cure, complete autonomic-neuroendocrine-immune route or durable regulatory set-point reset.

Isolate fish for two weeks, assemble 22 four-fish groups, score aggression after 24 hours, isolate the same individuals for two more weeks and reassemble them. A group relationship is scored after six consecutive unretaliated aggressive acts. Compare each individual's rank and the group's linearity across the two assemblies.

The same weight-matched female cichlids usually form linear hierarchies in repeated assemblies, yet only 27.3% of the 22 groups retain an identical rank ordering. Both persistent structural form and variable individual placement matter; rank is not a fixed intrinsic label.

Compare isolated pairwise round-robin encounters with simultaneous group assembly after two weeks of isolation. Four- and five-fish cohorts are weight matched. Round-robin dominance uses 15 consecutive acts in small encounter tanks; assembled-group scoring uses six acts after 24 hours in a larger tank. Preserve group-size-specific cohorts and repeated encounter histories.
Social access is changed through isolated round-robin encounters versus simultaneous group assembly, with different timing, tanks and dominance criteria retained as part of each protocol.

Assemblies of four and five cichlids yield substantially more linear hierarchies than the corresponding isolated pairwise protocols. Prior-attribute variation remains present, so this does not show that interaction alone is sufficient or identify the unique winner, loser or bystander pathway.

Fast one of 20 tested bats for 24 hours, return it to fed cage-mates and record two hours of behavior and mass change. Across 48 trial days over two years, score directed mouth-licking bouts, independent-day grooming and microsatellite relatedness. Compare dyadic transfer predictors and recurring network ties; preserve repeated bats and dyads.

In the captive mixed-relatedness preparation, food received from a partner predicts food donated to that partner, alongside grooming and donor-sex effects. This is an association in repeated dyads, not a randomized test of partner reciprocity or a human contract.

Sharing networks are more similar than the randomized comparison across eight-day and six-month separations. This supports bounded persistence of relationships within the tested colony, without demonstrating independence from all current members or survival after complete replacement.

The reported within-round and previous-day comparisons find no significant general increase in donating after a bat has itself been fed. Exact absolute amounts given and received across trials are not significantly correlated; this is not strict short-term tit-for-tat matching or equivalence of every reciprocity account.

Donors initiate most classified non-maternal sharing bouts; recipient age/forearm size do not significantly predict donations. These outcomes constrain harassment as a sole explanation in this colony, without excluding every solicitation process or directly measuring reproductive benefit.

Train two resident males in each of five subpopulations to open one physical side of a food puzzle, retaining three untrained-demonstrator controls. Release demonstrators and log RFID visits and door-direction solutions over 20 exposure days. Both techniques remain available and equally rewarded; independently sampled feeder associations enter network-diffusion analyses.

The experimental input introduces two resident demonstrators trained on blue/right or red/left food-puzzle opening, compared with pairs given no technique training; both opening directions then remain available.

Local uptake is faster and greater in seeded areas, and solutions preferentially use the introduced physical technique; controls show no consistent side bias. This supports a preparation-bound effect of demonstrator seeding, with geographic control placement retained as a design limitation.

Observed associations and acquisition order favor the fitted social-transmission model; first techniques disproportionately match the locally common variant. Conformist copying is a source-supported statistical interpretation, rather than direct measurement of belief, sanctions or a uniquely identified learning algorithm.

Reinstall food puzzles for five days at T1, T3 and C1 after nine months without apparatus access and without training new demonstrators. Distinguish birds previously present or previously solving from new participants. Approximately 40% of each subpopulation were present in the previous year; retain limited surviving sites and a device failure affecting one site.

After nine months, the two revisited seeded sites retain their earlier technique bias while both prior and inexperienced birds solve the reintroduced puzzle. Surviving trained/knowledgeable birds and a supplied reward remain available; memory and social transmission are compatible explanations, not proven member-independent persistence.

Introduce alumina mimics bearing blank solvent treatment, seed-associated oleic acid, colony-matched forager hydrocarbons or both odor classes. Compare three-minute outgoing trail counts before and after addition, excluding an immediate transient decline and using the reported multiple-testing correction. Preserve within-colony repeated treatments and the two field seasons.

Field nests receive the same type of inert mimic with combined forager/seed-associated odor, isolated odor classes or blank treatment; outgoing traffic is measured after the immediate handling transient.

Combined forager and seed-associated odor mimics increase outgoing trail counts in the reported field assay. This is a task-specific response to the supplied combination, not proof of a universal colony computation or receptor-level chemical mechanism.

The blank, seed-odor-only and forager-odor-only treatments have no significant measured pre/post outflow increase. Finite nulls constrain the tested combination account without establishing exact zero effects, biochemical synergy or universally necessary cue classes.

Observe unobstructed trajectories beneath a transparent entrance ceiling before and after blank mimics, then at least an hour later combined-odor mimics. Score contacts within an antenna length and distinguish contacts with ants versus mimics. Twenty focal foragers per treatment/colony are sampled before or after; preserve the fixed blank-before-combination order.

Foragers contact combined-odor mimics more than blank mimics, while contacts with ants decrease and total ant-plus-mimic contacts show no significant pre/post change. The response concerns contact composition and cannot be reduced to a universal increase in interaction rate.

Add seeds near a foraging trail and select low- and high-return-rate windows. Track unobstructed outgoing ants through the vestibule, score encounters and fit pooled changes in encounter frequency before each departure. Compare colonies and interaction classes while retaining that every focal ant eventually leaves the nest.

Among observed ants that leave the nest, interaction frequency rises during the seconds preceding departure, with colony- and return-rate-dependent magnitudes. These selected trajectories support temporal association, while threshold necessity requires observing comparably exposed ants that do not depart.

Reported low/high return-rate comparisons do not significantly change the interaction change-point time; density-normalized rate changes are also not significant in one colony. A common all-colony numerical activation threshold is not established.

Prevent incoming foragers from reaching the nest for three or ten minutes, retaining 22 trials after two technical exclusions and repeated observations per colony. Count returning/outgoing trail traffic and vestibule occupants every 30 seconds before, during and after interruption. Removed ants are released after the experiment.
The source interrupts returning foragers for three versus ten minutes in repeated field-colony trials, retaining both trail-flow and vestibule-occupancy measurements.

After the longer interruption, outgoing foraging resumes more slowly and vestibule depletion persists longer than after the shorter interruption. This is finite recovery in an existing colony; neither a universal resilience optimum nor irreversible regime change is measured.

Minimum vestibule occupancy does not significantly differ between three- and ten-minute interruption conditions; the reported post-interruption occupancy increase rates also do not significantly differ. Different recovery readouts must remain separate and nonsignificance is not equivalence.

Train separate fish sets to blue or yellow targets; combine six trained fish for one target with five for the other and add zero, five or ten untrained fish. Randomize blocks and majority-target identity, retain spontaneous yellow preference and repeated use of fish across days. No food is present during tests. Score the first fish arriving within two body lengths of a target as the shoal's operational choice.

The experiment holds the six-versus-five trained target groups fixed while adding zero, five or ten untrained fish, separately testing whether the spontaneous yellow preference belongs to the minority or majority.

When five yellow-trained fish oppose six blue-trained fish, added untrained fish increase the frequency of first arrivals at the blue majority target. This is a conditional shoal-choice result, not evidence that ignorance improves truth, welfare or human democratic institutions.

When yellow-trained fish already form the numerical majority, the reported added-untrained-fish effect is nonsignificant. The contrast excludes an unconditional rule that adding untrained participants always improves majority alignment.

Read the source's defined attraction/alignment/repulsion model and adaptive-network overview, with fixed informational subpopulations and differing preference strengths. Keep published simulations and bifurcation interpretation separate from fish trials; no parameter sweep, code execution or analytic derivation is independently replayed.

The published models yield a preference- and composition-dependent shift between minority and majority target control. Excessive uncommitted membership can weaken that effect as noise dominates. These are unreplayed model results with assumed local rules, distinct from measured fish behavior.

Association, aggression-defined rank, voluntarily conferred prestige, task specialization, recurring technique and explicit obligation denote different relations. Their shared placement in a social category does not establish common mechanisms or a universal individual-to-collective ontological transition.

Animal social organization is represented through finite, species-specific relational observations and interventions: cichlid aggression-defined hierarchy, vampire-bat sharing ties, bird foraging traditions, fish target choices and harvester-ant foraging regulation. These differ in membership, history, resources and observed times. Group structure and individual differences can both matter, while a common emergent substance, universal neural prerequisite, purely decentralized architecture and member-independent persistence are not established.

Aggression-defined dominance, influence, learned competence, worker task and voluntarily conferred human prestige are distinguished rather than treated as interchangeable rank. Cichlid experiments support context-sensitive hierarchy formation and changing individual positions. They do not establish human authority, obligation, responsibility, durable positions surviving complete occupant replacement or one hierarchy required by all social coordination.

Repeated social practice is a descriptive category for temporally recurring coordinated actions, with experimentally seeded bird foraging techniques and recurring bat-sharing ties as bounded animal examples. Technique transmission and nine-month retention do not establish every human practice, explicit expectations, automatic conflict reduction or universal dependence on hierarchy. Original practice-theory books remain attributed as unread conceptual sources.

Physical resource transfer, task-specific food acquisition and normative human exchange are represented separately. Captive bat studies provide observed food-sharing relationships and competing explanations; ant studies provide supplied-cue and return-flow interventions, not measurements of a complete social metabolism. Redistribution, obligations, institutions, queueing and scalability remain conceptual or unresolved unless their own source-bound observations support them.

Collective choice is operationalized by a declared group endpoint rather than a single universal aggregation rule. Golden-shiner experiments vary untrained membership against fixed, conflicting target-training groups and distinguish a preference-dependent effect from a reversed-target null. Published spatial/network models and social-choice concepts remain separate from fish observations. First arrival, majority alignment, consensus, truth, legitimacy and future group coordination are different quantities.

The colony category organizes experimentally perturbed harvester-ant foraging, local cue composition, observed departure timing and duration-dependent recovery. It does not combine all insect taxa, castes, task types and times into one measured colony organism. Foraging traffic, contacts and vestibule occupancy retain their own endpoints and nulls; chemical dose, necessary encounter threshold, complete feedback closure, construction, reproduction and colony-level irreducibility remain unestablished by these preparations.
Forty randomly assembled three-person teams complete sampled group tasks and a checkers criterion during sessions lasting up to five hours; individual reasoning is measured separately.
The source reports correlated task performance and a dominant extracted factor predicting a separate criterion; this is a fitted psychometric pattern, not proof of an irreducible group mind.

The second study recruits 579 participants in 152 teams, with group sizes two to five, a broader task sample and an architectural-design criterion. Measures and site/task subsets remain distinct from the first study.

The source reports a dominant fitted factor and criterion prediction across these sampled teams; modest pooled individual-IQ associations and correlational social-sensitivity results prevent independence-from-individuals or causal sex-composition claims.

Twelve sessions of twelve participants answer six factual questions over five estimation rounds, comparing no-feedback, aggregate-feedback and full-estimate feedback conditions with accuracy incentives and no reward for agreement.
Participants revise factual estimates with aggregate feedback, full feedback or no feedback, while rewards favor accuracy rather than matching peers.

The reported feedback contrasts combine reduced diversity with no matching collective-error improvement and increased subjective confidence. A slight error decline, particularly with aggregate feedback, is also reported: this is not a zero-effect or universally harmful-influence result. These endpoints are not interchangeable.

Participants coordinate on a face name through repeated random pairings with financial matching incentives; after a convention forms, introduce a committed minority promoting an alternative and compare five pairs of groups with different minority fractions.
The source varies the fraction of committed confederates after an experimentally established naming convention, retaining a pairwise matching-payoff procedure.

Larger committed minorities overturn the established name in the tested matched trial pairs, while smaller ones fail within the observation window. The approximately 25% transition is not a universal social constant.

Assign buyer and seller roles randomly, give private value/cost cards, permit public verbal bids/offers and acceptances during repeated short trading periods, and record executed contract prices and quantities under stated rule/schedule variants.

The article reports conditional convergence and rule/schedule-sensitive prices in constructed classroom auctions. Decentralized bids operate inside researcher-defined institutions; they do not establish organization-free or universally stable markets.

Subjects privately allocate integer tokens between a fixed-return market and a group-dependent CPR, receiving cash earnings. After an initial block without communication, the high-endowment one-shot design permits one ten-minute discussion; distinct repeated-communication designs permit discussion after subsequent rounds in low- and high-endowment environments. Individual investments remain anonymous and only aggregate investments reveal defections.

The final article reports improved CPR yields and agreements during communication phases without an external participant-enforcement authority. One-shot gains decay; repeated-discussion results depend on endowment and retain verbal reproach. This establishes a bounded possibility, not guaranteed governance or absence of every enforcement mechanism.

Unlike the anonymous-investment communication design, individual decisions are displayed under subject numbers throughout. After ten initial rounds introduce a costly option to fine another participant, varying fee/fine schedules across experiments; experimenters privately account for fees and fines.

The final article's sanction-only designs distinguish higher CPR yield from earnings after fees and fines; costly and misdirected sanctions substantially reduce the apparent gain. Monitoring, sanction availability, sanction targeting and cost accounting are separate features, not a universally effective enforcement mechanism.
After ten initial rounds, impose one ten-minute discussion and the opportunity to fine peers. Retain each group's stated strategy, subsequent investments and sanction costs as distinct trajectories.

Three groups with discussion and fines show different strategy, compliance and cost outcomes. One maintains its agreement without exercising fines, while a group without a clear agreement spends heavily on them. Nominal availability of the same components does not guarantee equivalent whole-group performance.

Recruit from the prior imposed-sanction pool. In four experiments permit discussion and majority choice of a sanction mechanism after an initial block; in two additional experiments provide that opportunity at the outset. Track choices, prior fee/fine experience and later yields separately.

The source's voluntarily chosen sanction institutions coexist with high reported yields in selected groups, but adoption correlates with prior institutional experience and differs by timing. This is evidence for historical and selection boundaries, not a randomized theorem that chosen sanctions cause cooperation.

Compare reported city-level social, economic and infrastructure indicators with population under the source's urban delineations. The selected reading does not reconstruct sampling years, boundary harmonization or regression fitting.

The source reports different aggregate scaling patterns for urban socioeconomic and infrastructure measures. The selected passages support a source-specific statistical report, without universal exponent, causal necessity or autonomous-city claims.

Reaggregate small statistical units into settlements and functional areas using alternative density/commuting thresholds; compare fitted urban-indicator relationships and patent population-cutoff sensitivity.

The source finds that several urban scaling conclusions change with city demarcation and patent population cutoff; many indicators are near-linear. A single population count therefore does not identify a universal urban mechanism.

Use the same monetary public-goods rules across pools: twenty-token individual endowment and return of 0.4 tokens to each member per contributed token. Compare ten fixed-group rounds without punishment with ten rounds permitting simultaneous peer deduction points after contribution feedback; each point costs the punisher one token and reduces its target's earnings by three.

The main article reports variable antisocial punishment, defined relative to the punisher's contribution, and variable contribution gains when punishment is available: eleven pools have at least weakly significant gains and five lack significant gains. Antisocial punishment is associated with weaker gains; nonsignificance does not establish a zero effect or a uniquely proven motive.

Relate laboratory punishment expenditures to externally compiled World Values Survey civic-cooperation measures and a rule-of-law indicator, adjusting for stated contributions, period and participant characteristics in source-reported regressions.

The source reports lower antisocial punishment in participant pools from countries with stronger measured civic-cooperation norms and rule of law. These contextual associations do not establish a randomized cultural cause or representative societal behavior.

Hayek's selected argument distinguishes dispersed local knowledge from a planner's fully given data. This is a conceptual account of the coordination problem, not experimental proof that every market is efficient or every centralized institution impossible.

The 1945 Charter constitutes named organs and distinguishes the General Assembly's deliberative/recommendation functions and voting procedure. These are documentary rule definitions, not observed governance performance.

The selected 1945 Charter articles distinguish Security Council responsibility, voting arrangements and contemplated measures. Transnational institutional design can contain asymmetric authority and enforcement powers; it is not simply decentralized voluntary consensus.

Human societal structures are a representation of specified relations, institutions and spatial aggregations, not one experimentally isolated ordering substance. Historical constitutive rules and observational urban indicators offer different evidence. Persistence across office holders, generations, territories and social strata needs its own longitudinal sampling; none is proved merely by calling society a pattern.

Collective intelligence denotes task-bound group-performance structure or accuracy under specified aggregation, not a single group mind. The two Woolley laboratory cohorts supply fitted cross-task patterns; Lorenz's feedback experiment supplies a contrary case where convergence and confidence do not deliver matching collective improvement. Group composition, interaction, aggregation and inference metrics remain separate.

A convention is represented through the particular coordination and incentive setting in which it is observed; a moral or prescriptive norm is not identical to naming agreement. The naming experiment supplies finite adoption successes/failures after a committed minority is introduced, while punishment records show that sanctions need not improve cooperation. Shared expectations, reputation, exclusion and moral obligation need separate measurements.

Market dynamics are reconstructed as transactions under explicitly supplied trading rules, values and information. Smith's classroom auctions provide conditional price/volume behavior; Hayek supplies a separate conceptual dispersed-knowledge argument. Neither is a complete model of production, financial crisis, trust, macroeconomic stability or a universal decentralized social regime.

Governance structures are represented as named constitutive offices, decision procedures and specified powers, separately from measured cooperation or realized authority. The original Charter supplies a documentary institutional example; common-pool experiments distinguish communication, monitoring, sanction costs, combined institutional trajectories and historically selected sanction choices. Definitions of jurisdiction or legitimacy do not themselves establish effective compliance or a universal route from informal norms to states.

Institutional change is a source-bounded historical question about specified rules, offices, practices and their alteration. A constitutive document defines continuity and powers; short laboratory treatments reveal different outcomes under nominally similar institutions, sanction costs and prior-experience-dependent selection. These supply neither intergenerational reproduction, universal path dependence, an autonomous institutional force nor one constructor for law, religion, education, science and finance.

Cities are operational spatial/population aggregations whose observed indicators and scaling depend on the national system, boundary, cutoff and proxy. Source-reported urban regularities are retained together with boundary-sensitive contrary evidence. Morphological formation, transport, segregation, infrastructure inertia and causal urban feedback need distinct data; no autonomous urban attractor, biological identity or universal growth law is inferred from aggregate correlations.

Cooperation, sanctions, organized conflict and violence are distinct observables. Selected published public-goods/common-pool results constrain universal enforcement stories: communication can support bounded agreements, fines have costs and variable outcomes, institutional choices retain prior experience and antisocial punishment accompanies weaker contribution gains. Country background is observational. These games do not reconstruct wars, large alliances, political mobilization, intergenerational rivalry or a common society-wide regulatory dynamic.

Transnational governance is reconstructed through specific historical constitutive organs, procedures and powers, rather than an undifferentiated global object. The 1945 Charter distinguishes organizational design, sovereign-member principles and asymmetric decision/enforcement provisions. These definitions differ from current amended rules, observed compliance, legitimacy, democratic authority and causal effectiveness; the original interdependence/regime works retain their actual reading boundaries.

Compare the authors' stated rationale and summary for diffusion models with heterogeneous influence and susceptibility. Complete network generation, parameter sweeps and numerical results remain outside this selected reading.

The authors report that highly influential individuals dominate only under selected model conditions; other modeled cascades depend mainly on the availability of susceptible ordinary individuals. This is conditional computational evidence, not a measured universal elite or an identified human transmission mechanism.

Participants learn written labels for 27 color/shape/motion pictures and produce labels for seen and unseen items. A learner's final output supplies the next learner's language. The seen set is sampled without the later ambiguity-removal filter.
Repeated transmission becomes more learnable while labels collapse onto multiple meanings.

Participants learn written labels for 27 color/shape/motion pictures and produce labels for seen and unseen items. A learner's final output supplies the next learner's language. Before each learner is trained, duplicate labels are restricted to one pictured meaning in the seen set.
Removing ambiguous training pairs changes the emerging structure: improved transmission coexists with more systematic signal-meaning correspondences.

Randomly assign a message displaying friends' voting faces, an informational message without those faces, or no message. Compare clicks between the two message arms; compare validated turnout in the voter-record-matched subset. The no-message group lacks both clickable response options.
The two message arms share the voting invitation, polling link and voting button; one additionally displays sampled profile pictures of friends who clicked the button.

The social message produces larger button/link responses and greater validated turnout than the informational-only arm in the source comparisons. Platform expression, information seeking and matched-record turnout remain separate measurements.

Informational-only versus no-message turnout is not significantly different in the reported matched-record comparison; this finite null is not equivalence or proof that every information campaign is ineffective.

At comment creation, randomly add one up-vote, one down-vote or no vote. Track first-viewer voting and accumulated scores; user impressions include the current score and comments are not sorted by popularity. The same users can contribute multiple outcomes.
The website randomly changes a comment's initial visible rating by plus one, minus one or zero while content quality is balanced in expectation.
Positive score seeding increases first-viewer approval and later mean ratings in the reported contrasts; effects differ by content topic.

Downward seeding elicits both negative responses and offsetting positive votes; the source reports no significant final-mean score difference from control. Some topic-specific positive-treatment contrasts also show no detected herding.

Use comparatively irrelevant classifications to distinguish in-group and out-group in allocations of rewards/penalties. Only the abstract's experimental description is available here; exact cohorts, schedules and allocation rules are unknown within this reading.

The abstract reports in-group favoritism under minimal categorization. This supplies a bounded behavioral contrast with explicit access limits, not evidence that all affiliation produces conflict or persists across generations.

Participants believe two computer-controlled players are real. Scans always proceed from watching because of a stated technical problem, to inclusion, to explicit exclusion after seven throws; explicit exclusion occurs only once. Measure BOLD and post-exclusion distress, with no distress report after the first scan.

The paper reports larger ACC response during explicit exclusion than inclusion and a positive distress association; RVPFC response is negatively associated with distress. These are ordered-task imaging contrasts and correlations, with the source's stated control limitations.

The reported ACC mediation concerns statistical relations among imaging and distress measures. No selective ACC/RVPFC intervention, matched physical-pain task or chronic institutional manipulation identifies a unique social-to-neural causal mechanism.

Interview 100 not-yet-committed registered voters in five precincts during September-October 1968; compare stated important issues with categorized contemporaneous local/national news emphasis. Exposure and issue salience are observed rather than randomly assigned.

Aggregate issue priorities in selected media and the restricted voter sample correspond strongly in the source analysis. This observational association does not alone identify media-to-public causation, a universal information environment or an opinion/accuracy effect.

Compare task/questionnaire measures of social orientation and cognitive style among three sampled groups; fit separate cultural/demographic and proposed transmission models, retaining cross-sectional sampling and exploratory analyses.

The source reports distinct group patterns across collectivism, closeness and attribution measures rather than one uniform shift; some second-generation measures are intermediate, others align with one comparator. The corrected closeness-table identity is retained.

Self-enhancement, categorization and the drawing task show no detected cultural-group difference in the source analysis. These finite nulls oppose a blanket all-trait shift, without establishing equivalence or cultural immutability.

Link fact-checker-veracity labels to reconstructed retweet cascades and compare depth, breadth, size and spread times, with reported covariate/bot sensitivity analyses. Truth labels and content are not randomly assigned.

False-classified rumors have faster and broader sampled diffusion than true-classified rumors in the source's reported comparisons. This is an observational difference with an explicit external veracity criterion, not a law that falsehood always wins.

Novelty/topic-distance and reply-word emotion measures accompany the cascade differences. They do not directly measure each sharer's belief, conscious motive or an isolated novelty-mediated causal pathway; removing classified bots is a sensitivity analysis, not randomized bot exposure.

Within the Republican experiment, use blocked random assignment to an offer of financial incentives to follow a bot carrying opposing-party messages for one month, versus control. Re-survey policy attitudes and monitor imperfect compliance; intent-to-treat and model-based complier estimates differ.

Within the Democratic experiment, use blocked random assignment to an offer of financial incentives to follow a bot carrying opposing-party messages for one month, versus control. Re-survey policy attitudes and monitor imperfect compliance; intent-to-treat and model-based complier estimates differ.
The Republican cohort is randomly offered incentives to follow a bot distributing liberal opinion-leader content; the actual exposure/compliance is imperfect and postassignment.

The source reports a conservative-direction intent-to-treat effect on the policy scale for the Republican cohort after the month; causal interpretation concerns the randomized incentivized offer, with stronger complier estimates requiring additional assumptions.
The Democratic cohort has a nonsignificant liberal-direction estimate in the source's reported exposure comparison. This is a finite null, not equality or a universal partisan asymmetry.

Cultural change is represented through finite learner-to-learner language experiments and measure-specific migrant profiles, with historical cultural theory retained as bibliographic context. Transmission fidelity, structural alignment, task expressivity, cohort association and conditional transmission-model fit are different observables. These cases do not establish one historical evolutionary regime, a universal cultural replicator or an inevitable progression from institutions to language.

Digital-network evidence separates randomized platform messages and score displays from observational rumor diffusion and conditional diffusion models. A site definition, one platform's experimental effect, a reconstructed retweet cascade and an inferred influence mechanism remain distinct. No universal recommendation algorithm, self-stabilizing digital regime or necessary cognitive hierarchy is established.

Influence is represented through specific randomized exposure effects and a separately declared diffusion-model report. A following/friendship link, visible popularity, an estimated treatment effect and a persistent directed influence coefficient are not interchangeable. Network stabilization, generalized brokerage advantage and a universal influential elite remain unestablished.

Knowledge valuation is a declared scope for attention, assessment and credibility processes, illustrated here by randomized public-rating effects and externally fact-checked diffusion. Approval, visibility, reputation, truth and evidential warrant remain distinct. Historical sociology/philosophy is bibliographic context; a common decentralized market mechanism across science, media, education and policy is not measured.

Cultural propagation is represented through changing laboratory language outputs and fact-checked platform cascades. A chosen content variant, its observable transmission, a reconstructed cascade and the hypothesis of a self-replicating meme retain separate roles. Variation and retention can be studied without admitting a universal memetic unit, fixed cultural fitness or source-independent replication mechanism.

Social identity is represented through a bounded minimal-categorization allocation report, differentiated migrant affiliation/orientation profiles and an acute exclusion imaging task. Behavioral allocation, questionnaire affiliation, cultural-group classification and distress/BOLD are different measurements. These sources do not establish one persistent social-system identity property, necessary national symbolism or unavoidable out-group conflict.

The proposed societal-to-neural link is bounded here by acute ordered social-exclusion imaging and an already admitted rat maternal-environment observation and mediation hypothesis. Social context, reported distress, BOLD, chromatin profiles and long-term neural plasticity retain different populations, times and evidence types. No direct universal downward/diagonal causal law, chronic institutional control variable or minimum neural carrier is established.

Shared information environments are represented as source-specific distributions of media salience, visible platform cues and fact-checked rumor exposure. The Chapel Hill media/public correlation, randomized platform response and observational diffusion are different preparations. A societal attractor, common credibility field, centralized-control independence or fixed sociogenetic construction order remains a hypothesis rather than a measured system state.

Transculturation is a declared historical-cultural research scope, illustrated by heterogeneous migrant-group profiles and bounded laboratory reorganization of transmitted labels. A mixed or intermediate measurement does not alone prove reciprocal historical transformation, creation of a novel tradition or irreducibility to cultural sources. Colonial power, unequal contact and adaptation claims require separately identified historical evidence.

The proposed mass-distortion regime remains a hypothesis bounded by fact-check-defined diffusion, randomized rating bias, a numerical-estimation feedback experiment and partisan attitude responses. A factual error, preference, ideological extremity, approval score, retweet and confidence judgment are distinct. No persistent societal attractor, common cognitive pathology or universal network-amplification mechanism is established.
